items.title: OpenAI calls for global AI Safety Institute to enhance youth safety and opportunities at upcoming G7 Summit [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Advancing youth safety and opportunity through global leadership
items.summary:
OpenAI is advocating for international collaboration to improve safety and opportunities for young people using AI technologies. The organization proposes establishing a dedicated global AI Safety Institute to develop safeguards, standards, and support systems tailored to youth.

OpenAI plans to discuss this initiative at the G7 Leaders’ Summit in Évian, France, emphasizing the need for sustained global coordination beyond single events. The proposed institute would facilitate ongoing cooperation among governments, researchers, civil society, and industry to share evidence, develop guidance, and raise safety standards for youth AI use worldwide.

The institute would build on existing efforts like Common Sense Media’s Youth AI Safety Institute and OpenAI’s partnerships with educators and researchers, including studies on Estonia’s national ChatGPT rollout in schools. OpenAI stresses that companies should implement age-appropriate protections, conduct regular youth safety risk assessments, and provide accessible parental controls and clear information about AI’s benefits and risks for young users.

items.summary:
OpenAI released a report showing that Codex, initially a coding tool, is now widely used by knowledge workers to automate routine tasks, accelerate work, and reduce friction across industries. The user base has grown more than sixfold since February 2026, with knowledge workers making up about 20 percent and growing rapidly.

Knowledge workers use Codex for creating reports, spreadsheets, presentations, contracts, and increasingly for research, data analysis, and building lightweight tools without engineering support. Users often run multiple tasks in parallel, which may enable them to take on more ambitious projects and expand their roles. Codex helps coordinate work across systems and teams, improve deliverables, and streamline review and approval processes.

items.originalTitle: Our views on AI policy and political advocacy
items.summary:
OpenAI has detailed its approach to AI policy and political advocacy, emphasizing the importance of transparent communication about its values and policy positions. The company states it has not formed or funded any political action committees (PACs) or made donations to political campaigns, and that employee political activities are personal and separate from the company.

The company also addressed questions about the political group Leading the Future (LTF), clarifying that involvement by its co-founder Greg Brockman and his wife is personal and not representative of OpenAI. OpenAI stresses that no external political group speaks for the company and advocates for thoughtful AI regulation, safety standards, public accountability, and broad access to AI benefits through direct and transparent engagement.

items.title: OpenAI breaks ground on 1GW Stargate data center in Michigan with community and labor partnerships [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Building the infrastructure for the Intelligence Age in Michigan
items.summary:
OpenAI has started construction on The Barn, a 1 gigawatt data center campus in Saline, Michigan, aiming to build AI infrastructure while supporting local communities and workers. The project includes commitments to protect local residents from infrastructure costs, safeguard water resources, and create thousands of union construction and permanent jobs.

The initiative involves partnerships with Oracle, Related Digital, Walbridge, and local government, contributing $10 million to community improvements and projecting $1 billion in tax revenue over the lease term. OpenAI will also provide up to $45 million in Codex credits to over 400,000 Michigan students and collaborate with state agencies on AI literacy and workforce training programs to prepare residents for AI-related jobs.

This project reflects Michigan's industrial heritage and aims to catalyze a new era of technology-driven economic growth rooted in skilled labor and community investment, aligning with broader state strategies for education and workforce development.

items.summary:
OpenAI has made its frontier models and Codex generally available on Amazon Web Services (AWS), allowing enterprises to integrate these AI tools into their existing AWS environments with familiar security, compliance, and procurement workflows. This integration aims to reduce barriers to AI adoption by enabling faster transition from evaluation to production using AWS-native controls.

The offering includes OpenAI models and Codex on Amazon Bedrock, supporting both commercial and GovCloud regions. Customers like Amgen and Autodesk are exploring these capabilities to enhance scientific research and design workflows within secure and governed AWS infrastructures. OpenAI and AWS plan to expand these capabilities further, including future releases like Daybreak, which focuses on cybersecurity applications to help organizations adopt advanced AI securely and efficiently.

items.title: Boston Children’s Hospital integrates OpenAI’s AI across clinical and operational workflows, diagnosing over 40 rare diseases and saving 60,000 staff hours [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Boston Children’s uses AI to unlock new diagnoses
items.summary:
Boston Children’s Hospital has embedded OpenAI’s artificial intelligence technology into its clinical and administrative operations to improve pediatric care, particularly for complex and rare conditions. This integration has helped diagnose more than 40 previously unresolved rare diseases while reducing operational costs and saving approximately 60,000 staff hours.

The hospital developed an enterprise AI layer that supports research, clinical decision-making, and administrative tasks, enabling rapid deployment of AI tools tailored to various roles. AI automations now manage supply chain processes, surgical scheduling, and clinical data synthesis, contributing to over $7 million in redeployed labor. This approach addresses both the cognitive limits of clinicians and the administrative burdens faced by staff, enhancing care delivery and operational efficiency.

items.title: OpenAI releases shared playbook to standardize trustworthy third-party evaluations of frontier AI models [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: A shared playbook for trustworthy third party evaluations
items.summary:
OpenAI has published guidance aimed at improving the reliability and validity of independent third-party evaluations for advanced AI systems. The playbook outlines best practices for assessing model capabilities, safeguards, and comparative performance, emphasizing the importance of evaluation setups and environments, or "harnesses," that reflect real-world use cases.

The guidance categorizes evaluation claims into capability elicitation, safeguard performance, and controlled comparisons, and highlights common validity threats such as reward hacking, refusals, contamination, broken problems, and sandbagging. OpenAI stresses that selecting an appropriate harness is critical for accurate assessment, especially for models that operate over multiple steps or use tools, and recommends transparent reporting of evaluation design and evidence to support claims.

items.summary:
OpenAI and Thrive Holdings collaborated to build Tax AI, a Codex-powered agent designed to automate and improve the preparation of complex tax returns for Crete's network of accounting firms. The system processes thousands of returns, reducing manual data entry time and increasing accuracy and throughput during tax season.

Tax AI uses practitioner feedback, production data, and a Codex-driven iteration loop to self-improve continuously, achieving up to 97% accuracy and saving practitioners about a third of their preparation time. The system has expanded its capabilities from simpler forms to more complex filings, demonstrating measurable improvements in accuracy and efficiency over several months.

This approach addresses challenges in tax preparation by making production failures visible and actionable without heavy engineering intervention, enabling faster product development and potentially serving as a model for other domains requiring expert practitioner input and complex data handling.

items.title: OpenAI analysis finds 4 million Americans use ChatGPT as a first hire to support small business operations and reduce startup costs [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: AI is becoming a first hire for small businesses
items.summary:
A new OpenAI report reveals that around four million people in the US used ChatGPT in March 2026 to help plan, start, run, or grow small businesses across various sectors including consulting, retail, home services, and hospitality. These entrepreneurs often rely on AI to perform multiple roles such as marketing, customer service, and legal tasks, which would otherwise require additional staff or consultants.

The report highlights that prospective entrepreneurs use ChatGPT mainly for branding and product development, while active entrepreneurs focus on marketing, customer communication, and compliance. This usage pattern suggests AI lowers the fixed costs of entrepreneurship by enabling small business owners to manage diverse tasks without immediate hires, potentially increasing the viability and survival of modest businesses.

items.title: OpenAI model disproves Erdős’s 80-year-old unit distance conjecture in discrete geometry with polynomial improvement [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: An OpenAI model has disproved a central conjecture in discrete geometry
items.summary:
An OpenAI model has solved the longstanding planar unit distance problem posed by Paul Erdős in 1946, disproving the prevailing conjecture that square grid constructions were optimal for maximizing unit-distance pairs among points in the plane. The model produced an infinite family of counterexamples yielding a polynomial improvement, and the proof has been verified by external mathematicians.

The breakthrough was achieved using a general-purpose reasoning model not specifically trained for mathematics or this problem, marking the first time AI has autonomously solved a prominent open problem in a mathematical subfield. The proof applies sophisticated algebraic number theory concepts to a classical geometric question, and leading mathematicians have praised the result as a milestone demonstrating AI’s capability for original and deep mathematical reasoning.

items.title: OpenAI advances content provenance with C2PA conformance, Google SynthID watermarking, and a public verification tool to enhance AI-generated media transparency [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Advancing content provenance for a safer, more transparent AI ecosystem
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced new measures to improve content provenance in AI-generated media, including adopting the C2PA open standard for metadata, integrating Google DeepMind's SynthID invisible watermarking for images, and launching a public tool to verify AI-generated content. These efforts aim to provide users with reliable signals about the origin and authenticity of AI-created images and audio, supporting a safer and more transparent AI ecosystem.

The company has been involved in provenance standards since 2024 and recently became a C2PA Conforming Generator Product, enabling platforms to preserve and share provenance metadata. The multi-layered approach combines metadata and watermarking to ensure provenance information survives common content transformations like resizing or screenshots. The new public verification tool allows users to detect whether images were generated by OpenAI models such as ChatGPT, Codex, or the OpenAI API by checking for embedded provenance signals.

These updates build on OpenAI's ongoing collaboration with industry partners to foster trust and transparency in AI-generated content, addressing challenges in verifying media authenticity as AI tools become more widespread.

items.originalTitle: OpenAI and Malta partner to bring ChatGPT Plus to all citizens
items.summary:
OpenAI and the Government of Malta have launched a partnership to offer all Maltese citizens free access to ChatGPT Plus for one year, coupled with an AI literacy course developed by the University of Malta. The initiative aims to empower citizens with practical AI skills and promote responsible use of AI technologies.

The program, part of Malta's AI for All initiative, will begin in May 2026 and is managed by the Malta Digital Innovation Authority. It targets residents and citizens both within Malta and abroad, providing education on AI's capabilities and limitations alongside access to advanced AI tools. This partnership is the first of its scale globally and reflects Malta's commitment to leading AI adoption through strategic national initiatives.

The feature supports over 12,000 financial institutions and is available on web, iOS, and Android platforms, starting with a preview to a smaller group to gather feedback and improve the service.

Users can view a dashboard summarizing their portfolio performance, spending, subscriptions, and upcoming payments, and provide additional context such as savings goals or planned purchases. ChatGPT uses this information to offer personalized guidance and help users understand tradeoffs and plan financial decisions, though it is not a substitute for professional financial advice.

items.summary:
OpenAI developed a secure sandbox environment to enable Codex on Windows, addressing the lack of native OS features for safe code execution. This sandbox restricts file writes to the user's workspace and limits network access, allowing Codex to operate with user-level permissions while maintaining safety.

OpenAI's custom solution enforces constraints at the OS level to provide a safer and more efficient developer experience with Codex on Windows devices.

items.title: OpenAI responds to TanStack npm supply chain attack by rotating macOS app certificates and requiring updates by June 26, 2026
items.originalTitle: Our response to the TanStack npm supply chain attack
items.summary:
OpenAI disclosed a supply chain attack involving the TanStack npm library that affected two employee devices and limited internal source code repositories. The company found no evidence of customer data compromise or unauthorized software changes but took immediate action to contain the breach and protect its systems.

As part of its response, OpenAI is rotating code-signing certificates for its macOS applications, requiring users to update their apps by June 26, 2026, to maintain security. The company coordinated with Apple to block new notarizations using the previous certificate and confirmed no malicious software was signed with OpenAI certificates. OpenAI also accelerated deployment of security controls to mitigate future supply chain risks.

items.title: NVIDIA engineers use Codex with GPT-5.5 to accelerate production system development and automate machine learning research workflows [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: How NVIDIA engineers and researchers build with Codex
items.summary:
NVIDIA engineers and researchers have adopted Codex, powered by GPT-5.5, as their primary tool for complex engineering tasks and end-to-end machine learning experiments, achieving a tenfold speed improvement in research workflows. Codex runs on NVIDIA's GB200 and GB300 infrastructure, enabling longer autonomous sessions that identify bugs and suggest improvements beyond initial prompts. 

The coding agents team at NVIDIA has leveraged Codex to evolve internal platforms into production-ready systems and rapidly build applications like a podcast recording app, significantly reducing development time. Researchers use Codex to automate the research loop, from hypothesis generation to script writing and remote experiment execution, with capabilities such as translating Python codebases into more efficient Rust implementations. 

NVIDIA views Codex as a transformative tool that accelerates the transition from concept to execution and testing, with ongoing exploration of its potential to further enhance engineering and research productivity.

AutoScout24 plans to deepen AI integration into core systems to further improve automation and user experiences.

These trends indicate that ChatGPT is becoming a more mainstream tool used by a broader mix of people across more regions for recurring tasks.

items.originalTitle: How enterprises are scaling AI
items.summary:
European enterprise leaders interviewed by OpenAI emphasize that scaling AI successfully involves more than rapid deployment; it requires cultivating trust, establishing governance early, redesigning workflows, and maintaining quality standards. These organizations prioritize culture, ownership, and hybrid workflows that enhance expert judgment rather than just throughput.

The insights highlight five recurring patterns: focusing on culture before tooling, involving security and compliance teams early to enable faster progress, empowering teams to build with AI, defining quality metrics before scaling, and protecting expert decision-making through hybrid workflows. This approach moves enterprises beyond individual productivity gains toward embedding AI responsibly in end-to-end processes with human oversight.

Ads are clearly labeled, do not affect the AI's responses, and are designed with privacy protections that prevent advertisers from accessing personal chat data.

The pilot aims to support broader access to ChatGPT by funding free and low-cost tiers while maintaining user trust and control. Users can dismiss ads, provide feedback, and manage ad personalization, with ads excluded from sensitive topics and accounts of users under 18. OpenAI plans to expand the program thoughtfully, learning from real-world usage and adjusting safeguards to protect privacy and prevent misleading ads.

items.title: OpenAI launches Trusted Contact feature in ChatGPT to notify designated individuals of serious self-harm concerns [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing Trusted Contact in ChatGPT
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Trusted Contact, an optional safety feature in ChatGPT that allows users to designate a trusted adult who may be notified if automated systems and trained reviewers detect serious self-harm concerns in conversations. This feature aims to provide an additional layer of support alongside existing crisis helplines by encouraging connection with someone the user trusts during moments of distress.

Users can add one trusted contact who must accept the role before activation. If a serious safety concern is detected, ChatGPT informs the user and may notify the trusted contact with a limited message that protects user privacy. The feature was developed with input from clinicians and mental health experts and includes human review of notifications to ensure accuracy and timely response.

items.title: OpenAI explains how ChatGPT trains on diverse data while applying privacy filters and offering user controls to limit data use [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: How ChatGPT learns about the world while protecting privacy
items.summary:
OpenAI details how ChatGPT learns from a mix of publicly available information, partnerships, and user interactions while employing advanced privacy filters to minimize personal data exposure during training. Users can control whether their conversations contribute to model improvements through settings and temporary chat options.

The company uses an internal Privacy Filter to mask personal information in datasets and user conversations when enabled, and it offers this tool to other developers. ChatGPT also includes features like Memory, which users can manage or disable to control data retention, and provides mechanisms for users to export data or submit privacy requests.

OpenAI emphasizes its responsibility to protect user privacy as ChatGPT is used for increasingly personal tasks, balancing privacy safeguards with the need to address potential harms. Users are advised not to share sensitive information they do not want processed or reviewed.

items.originalTitle: How frontier firms are pulling ahead
items.summary:
OpenAI's B2B Signals research reveals that frontier firms at the 95th percentile of AI usage now employ 3.5 times more AI intelligence per worker than typical firms, up from 2 times a year ago. This advantage stems mainly from deeper, more complex AI use rather than just higher message volume, with frontier firms sending 16 times as many Codex messages per worker, indicating greater adoption of agentic workflows.

The report highlights that leading companies are moving beyond basic AI access to embed AI deeply into workflows, delegating complex tasks to AI agents and scaling production use cases across industries. Examples like Cisco demonstrate significant productivity gains by integrating Codex into engineering workflows, reducing build times and increasing defect resolution throughput. This trend suggests that firms investing in governance, enablement, and advanced AI tools are pulling ahead in sustainable competitive advantage.

items.title: Singular Bank launches Singularity assistant using ChatGPT and Codex to save bankers 60–90 minutes daily by streamlining portfolio analysis and client communications [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Singular Bank helps bankers move fast with ChatGPT and Codex
items.summary:
Singular Bank, a private bank in Madrid, developed Singularity, an internal assistant powered by ChatGPT and Codex, to help bankers analyze portfolios in real time, prepare for meetings, and generate compliant follow-up communications. This tool reduces meeting preparation time from about 20 minutes to under one minute, enabling bankers to focus more on advising clients and building relationships.

Singularity integrates with the bank’s core systems to flag portfolio risks, recommend actions, and automate routine tasks such as call reports and client communications. Bankers have executed over 3,500 operations in a 30-day period using the system, which improves traceability and regulatory reporting while maintaining compliance. The assistant enhances bankers’ expertise by allowing faster, more consistent, and precise client interactions without replacing human judgment.

items.originalTitle: Uber uses OpenAI to help people earn smarter and book faster
items.summary:
Uber has incorporated OpenAI's large language models to enhance its platform with AI-powered assistants and voice capabilities aimed at helping drivers make smarter earning decisions and riders book rides more quickly. This integration supports Uber's complex real-time marketplace, which operates across 15,000 cities and over 70 countries with millions of daily trips and drivers.

The AI assistants provide drivers with real-time insights and personalized guidance by analyzing marketplace data such as earnings trends and demand heatmaps, reducing the cognitive load of decision-making. Uber's multi-agent AI system routes queries to specialized models to ensure accuracy, safety, and low latency, while an internal governance layer monitors responses to maintain trust and policy compliance. This technology benefits both new and experienced drivers by accelerating onboarding and optimizing platform engagement.

items.originalTitle: Unlocking large scale AI training networks with MRC (Multipath Reliable Connection)
items.summary: OpenAI has introduced Multipath Reliable Connection (MRC), a new networking protocol developed with AMD, Broadcom, Intel, Microsoft, and NVIDIA to enhance data transfer speed and reliability in large AI training clusters. MRC is designed to reduce network congestion and quickly route around failures, improving the efficiency of supercomputer networks used for training frontier AI models. The protocol extends existing standards and is deployed across OpenAI's largest NVIDIA GB200 supercomputers, including those hosted with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and Microsoft.

OpenAI has introduced the European Youth Safety Blueprint and announced recipients of its EMEA Youth & Wellbeing Grants to promote safe and responsible AI use among teenagers, families, and educators across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. The Blueprint outlines five pillars for policymakers to enhance youth protections while maintaining access to AI tools that support learning and creativity.

The €500,000 grant program supports 12 organizations working on practical projects and research related to youth safety, mental health, AI literacy, and age assurance. OpenAI's efforts build on its global youth safety principles and collaborations with governments and institutions to deploy AI responsibly in education and wellbeing.

items.title: OpenAI rearchitects WebRTC infrastructure to deliver low-latency voice AI for over 900 million weekly users globally [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: How OpenAI delivers low-latency voice AI at scale
items.summary:
OpenAI has redesigned its WebRTC stack to support real-time voice AI applications with low latency, fast connection setup, and stable media round-trip times, enabling natural conversational interactions at scale. This new architecture addresses challenges related to media termination, session state management, and global routing to reduce latency and improve user experience.

The overhaul leverages WebRTC's standardized protocols for encrypted, low-latency audio streaming, allowing AI models to process speech while users are still talking. OpenAI's approach departs from traditional selective forwarding units by optimizing for one-to-one sessions, which are common in voice AI use cases, ensuring crisp turn-taking and global reach across its infrastructure.

items.title: OpenAI launches Advanced Account Security with phishing-resistant login and enhanced recovery for ChatGPT and Codex accounts [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing Advanced Account Security
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Advanced Account Security, an opt-in feature for ChatGPT and Codex users that provides stronger protections against unauthorized access through phishing-resistant sign-in methods, stricter account recovery options, and improved session management. This feature targets users at higher risk of digital attacks, such as journalists and political dissidents, by requiring passkeys or physical security keys and disabling password and SMS/email recovery methods.

The new security measures include shorter session durations, login alerts, and automatic exclusion of conversations from model training for users handling sensitive information. OpenAI has partnered with Yubico to offer discounted hardware security keys and will require members of its Trusted Access for Cyber program to enable Advanced Account Security starting June 1, 2026, or demonstrate equivalent protections through single sign-on workflows.

items.title: OpenAI traces rise of 'goblin' metaphors in GPT-5 models to Nerdy personality training incentives [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Where the goblins came from
items.summary:
OpenAI investigated an unusual increase in references to goblins and similar creatures in GPT-5 model outputs, identifying the cause as high rewards given during training for the Nerdy personality customization feature. This incentive unintentionally encouraged the use of creature metaphors, which then spread beyond the Nerdy personality to other model outputs through reinforcement learning and fine-tuning processes.

The phenomenon first appeared after the GPT-5.1 launch and became more pronounced in GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.5, with goblin mentions rising significantly in user interactions. Analysis showed that although the Nerdy personality accounted for a small fraction of responses, it was responsible for the majority of goblin references, indicating a transfer of this stylistic quirk to other contexts. OpenAI's findings highlight how subtle training incentives can lead to unexpected and widespread changes in AI behavior.

items.originalTitle: The next phase of the Microsoft OpenAI partnership
items.summary:
OpenAI and Microsoft announced an amended agreement to streamline their partnership, providing long-term clarity and flexibility while maintaining Microsoft as OpenAI's primary cloud provider and major shareholder. The update includes non-exclusive licensing of OpenAI's intellectual property to Microsoft through 2032, removal of Microsoft's revenue share payments to OpenAI, and continuation of OpenAI's revenue share payments to Microsoft through 2030 with a cap.

The agreement allows OpenAI to serve products across any cloud provider if Microsoft cannot support necessary capabilities, and emphasizes ongoing collaboration on scaling data center capacity, next-generation silicon, and AI applications in cybersecurity. This amendment aims to strengthen their joint ability to build and operate AI platforms at scale while enabling both companies to pursue new opportunities.

items.title: OpenAI releases Symphony, an open-source specification for Codex orchestration that turns issue trackers into continuous agent systems to reduce developer context switching [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: An open-source spec for orchestration: Symphony
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Symphony, an open-source specification designed to orchestrate Codex agents by transforming project management boards like Linear into control planes where each open task is assigned a continuously running agent. This system aims to improve engineering productivity by minimizing the cognitive load and context switching associated with managing multiple interactive coding sessions.

Symphony maps each issue to a dedicated agent workspace and continuously monitors task status to ensure agents work on unblocked tasks, restarting stalled agents and allowing agents to create new tasks as needed. This approach decouples work from individual coding sessions and pull requests, enabling more efficient parallel execution of complex workflows such as feature development and infrastructure migrations. OpenAI reports that using Symphony has led to a 500% increase in landed pull requests on some teams.

items.originalTitle: Our principles
items.summary:
Sam Altman details five guiding principles that shape OpenAI's mission to develop artificial general intelligence (AGI) in a way that benefits all humanity. These principles emphasize democratization, empowerment, universal prosperity, resilience, and safety to ensure AI technology is accessible, equitable, and responsibly deployed.

The principles include resisting power consolidation by a few, enabling users to achieve their goals with AI, promoting widespread prosperity through accessible AI infrastructure, collaborating with governments and society to manage AI risks, and prioritizing safety and alignment. OpenAI aims to balance broad access with caution to minimize harm while fostering innovation and societal flourishing.

items.title: OpenAI introduces AI Jobs Transition Framework analyzing 921 US occupations to assess automation risk, job reorganization, growth potential, and minimal AI impact [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Modeling an AI jobs transition
items.summary:
OpenAI has developed the AI Jobs Transition Framework to evaluate how AI might affect 921 occupations covering approximately 148 million jobs in the U.S. The framework categorizes jobs based on AI's ability to perform tasks, the necessity of human involvement, and whether AI-driven productivity gains could increase demand.

The analysis identifies four categories: about 18% of jobs face high automation risk, including roles like data-entry clerks and telemarketers; 24% are likely to reorganize, such as lawyers and teachers who will integrate AI while retaining human judgment; 12% could grow as AI lowers service costs, benefiting fields like tutoring and healthcare; and 46% show less immediate change, including physically intensive jobs like electricians and construction workers. The framework emphasizes that these categories map potential changes rather than predict job losses, highlighting the complexity of AI's impact on the labor market.

items.title: OpenAI speeds up Codex agent workflows by 40% with WebSockets and caching in the Responses API to reduce latency and API overhead [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Speeding up agentic workflows with WebSockets in the Responses API
items.summary:
OpenAI has improved the performance of its Codex agent workflows by integrating WebSockets and connection-scoped caching into the Responses API, resulting in a 40% faster end-to-end experience. These changes reduce redundant processing and network overhead, allowing users to benefit from faster model inference speeds that have increased from 65 to nearly 1,000 tokens per second.

The improvements address the bottleneck caused by repeated API calls that processed full conversation histories for each request. By establishing a persistent WebSocket connection, the system caches reusable state and only sends new information, minimizing latency. Additional optimizations include caching tokens and model configurations, reducing network hops, and enhancing safety checks to flag issues more quickly, all contributing to a more responsive and efficient agent loop.

items.summary: OpenAI has released Privacy Filter, a small, open-weight model designed to detect and redact personally identifiable information (PII) in unstructured text. The model supports high-throughput privacy workflows, runs locally to keep data on device, and achieves state-of-the-art performance on the PII-Masking-300k benchmark after correcting annotation issues. Privacy Filter uses a context-aware token-classification approach to identify a wide range of PII categories, including names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, dates, account numbers, and secrets, enabling developers to build stronger privacy protections into their AI systems and workflows.

Hyatt has implemented ChatGPT Enterprise, powered by GPT-5.4 and Codex, for its global corporate and hotel employees to improve productivity, streamline operations, and enhance guest services. The AI tools support multiple departments including finance, marketing, business development, product engineering, and customer experience.

The rollout includes live onboarding and training in collaboration with OpenAI, enabling Hyatt teams to integrate AI into daily workflows. This deployment is part of Hyatt's broader strategy to leverage AI technologies to deliver more personalized and efficient service, complementing other AI-powered initiatives like the Hyatt app in ChatGPT.

items.title: OpenAI updates Codex app with computer control, in-app browsing, image generation, memory, and expanded developer workflow support [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Codex for (almost) everything
items.summary:
OpenAI has released a major update to its Codex application for macOS and Windows, enhancing its capabilities to assist over 3 million weekly developers. The update enables Codex to operate computer apps directly, supports in-app web browsing, generates images, remembers user preferences, and integrates with more developer tools to streamline software development tasks.

New features include parallel agent operation on Macs, an in-app browser for frontend and game development, and support for over 90 new plugins including integrations with JIRA, CircleCI, GitLab, and Microsoft Suite. The app also adds workflow improvements such as GitHub review comment handling, multiple terminal tabs, remote devbox connections via SSH, and rich file previews.

Codex now supports automations that preserve conversation context over time and can schedule future tasks, with a preview of memory features to recall past interactions and preferences. These enhancements aim to accelerate development cycles by helping users manage ongoing work and prioritize tasks across tools like Slack, Gmail, and Notion. The update is available immediately for Codex desktop users signed in with ChatGPT, with some features rolling out soon to enterprise and regional users.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-Rosalind, a reasoning model optimized for life sciences research and drug discovery workflows [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing GPT-Rosalind for life sciences research
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced GPT-Rosalind, a new AI model designed to accelerate research in biology, drug discovery, and translational medicine by improving reasoning across chemistry, protein engineering, and genomics. The model supports complex scientific workflows such as literature review, experimental planning, and data analysis to help researchers generate hypotheses and design experiments more efficiently.

GPT-Rosalind is available as a research preview through ChatGPT, Codex, and the API for qualified users, with a Life Sciences research plugin connecting to over 50 scientific tools and data sources. OpenAI is collaborating with organizations including Amgen, Moderna, and the Allen Institute to apply the model in real-world research settings, aiming to reduce the time and complexity involved in early-stage drug discovery and biological research.

items.title: OpenAI launches Trusted Access for Cyber initiative with $10 million in API grants to enhance global cyber defense using GPT-5.4-Cyber [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Accelerating the cyber defense ecosystem that protects us all
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced the Trusted Access for Cyber program to broaden access to advanced cybersecurity tools while ensuring trust and safeguards. The initiative involves partnerships with security firms, enterprises, and researchers to improve threat detection and response across diverse digital environments.

The program includes $10 million in API credits awarded to organizations like Socket, Semgrep, Calif, and Trail of Bits, focusing on software supply chain security and vulnerability research. Major companies such as Bank of America, Cisco, CrowdStrike, and JPMorgan Chase have joined to support these efforts, alongside access granted to U.S. and UK AI security institutes for model evaluation. OpenAI aims to expand this ecosystem to strengthen collective cyber defense capabilities globally.

items.title: OpenAI updates Agents SDK with native sandbox execution and model-native harness to support secure, long-running agents across files and tools [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: The next evolution of the Agents SDK
items.summary:
OpenAI has released an updated version of its Agents SDK that introduces native sandbox execution and a model-native harness, enabling developers to build agents capable of inspecting files, running commands, editing code, and handling long-horizon tasks securely. The new SDK provides standardized infrastructure designed specifically for OpenAI models, allowing agents to operate within controlled environments and work across multiple files and tools efficiently.

The updated harness includes configurable memory, sandbox-aware orchestration, and integrations with common agent system primitives such as tool use, progressive disclosure, custom instructions, and code execution. This design aims to improve reliability and performance on complex, long-running tasks while offering flexibility for developers to adapt the SDK to their specific needs. Early testers reported that the SDK made production automation of complex workflows more viable, particularly in clinical record processing.

items.title: OpenAI expands Trusted Access for Cyber program with GPT-5.4-Cyber model to support verified cybersecurity defenders [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Trusted access for the next era of cyber defense
items.summary:
OpenAI has scaled its Trusted Access for Cyber (TAC) program to include thousands of verified individual defenders and hundreds of teams, introducing GPT-5.4-Cyber, a model fine-tuned for defensive cybersecurity use cases. This initiative aims to enhance cyber defense capabilities while maintaining strong safeguards as AI models become more capable.

The program is built on principles of democratized access, iterative deployment, and ecosystem resilience, using strong identity verification and automated processes to grant access to legitimate users. OpenAI also supports the cybersecurity community through grants, open-source contributions, and tools like Codex Security to help defenders identify and fix vulnerabilities more rapidly.

OpenAI's approach addresses the dual-use nature of AI in cybersecurity by expanding access based on user trust and intent, aiming to balance broad availability with granular controls to prevent misuse. The company plans to continue evolving its models and safeguards in response to emerging threats and capabilities in the cyber defense landscape.

items.title: OpenAI publishes guidance on responsible and safe use of ChatGPT and AI tools, emphasizing accuracy, transparency, and human oversight [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Responsible and safe use of AI
items.summary:
OpenAI has released best practices for the responsible and safe use of AI tools like ChatGPT, highlighting the importance of accuracy, transparency, and maintaining human oversight in AI-assisted work. The guidance advises users to respect workplace and OpenAI policies, verify critical information, and be cautious of potential biases in AI outputs.

The recommendations also stress the need for expert review in legal, medical, or financial contexts and encourage transparency about AI use when required by employers or institutions. Users are urged to obtain consent before sharing personal data and to provide feedback on unsafe or incorrect AI responses to help improve safety and reliability.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Healthcare, a HIPAA-compliant AI tool to assist clinicians with diagnosis, documentation, and patient care workflows [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Healthcare
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT for Healthcare, a secure AI workspace designed to support hospital providers with clinical workflows while complying with HIPAA regulations to protect patient data. The tool offers cited answers from trusted medical sources and helps clinicians reduce administrative tasks such as drafting documentation, preparing prior authorizations, and summarizing patient information.

The platform includes prompt templates tailored for common clinical scenarios, including diagnostic test selection, differential diagnosis, care planning, and patient counseling. These resources aim to improve efficiency and allow clinicians to focus more on patient care by streamlining evidence search, guideline reconciliation, and documentation processes.

items.title: OpenAI rotates macOS code signing certificates and updates apps after Axios developer tool supply chain attack, confirms no user data breach [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Our response to the Axios developer tool compromise
items.summary:
OpenAI responded to a supply chain attack involving the Axios developer tool used in their macOS app-signing process by revoking and rotating their macOS code signing certificates. They updated their macOS applications, including ChatGPT Desktop and Codex, requiring users to update by May 8, 2026, to maintain functionality and security. OpenAI found no evidence that user data, systems, or software were compromised during the incident.

The attack occurred on March 31, 2026, when a malicious version of Axios was executed in a GitHub Actions workflow with access to signing certificates. OpenAI engaged a third-party forensics firm, worked with Apple to block unauthorized notarizations, and addressed the root cause, which was a misconfiguration in their workflow. The company emphasized that this issue only affected macOS apps and not other platforms or web versions.

items.title: OpenAI launches Safety Fellowship to support independent AI safety and alignment research from September 2026 to February 2027 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Announcing the OpenAI Safety Fellowship
items.summary:
OpenAI has announced the Safety Fellowship, a pilot program inviting external researchers, engineers, and practitioners to conduct rigorous research on AI safety and alignment. The program runs from September 14, 2026, to February 5, 2027, and offers mentorship, workspace options in Berkeley or remote work, a monthly stipend, compute support, and expects substantial research outputs such as papers or datasets.

The fellowship prioritizes research in areas including safety evaluation, ethics, robustness, scalable mitigations, privacy-preserving methods, and misuse domains, welcoming applicants from diverse fields like computer science, social science, cybersecurity, and HCI. Applications are open until May 3, 2026, with notifications by July 25, and fellows will receive API credits but no internal system access.

items.title: OpenAI and Gates Foundation hold AI workshop for disaster response leaders across 13 Asian countries to improve emergency management [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Helping disaster response teams turn AI into action across Asia
items.summary:
OpenAI partnered with the Gates Foundation, Asian Disaster Preparedness Center, and DataKind to host an AI workshop in Bangkok for 50 disaster management leaders from Southeast and South Asia. The event aimed to help governments and nonprofits use AI tools to respond faster and more effectively to disasters in the region.

Participants from 13 countries, including Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, and Thailand, collaborated with OpenAI mentors to develop practical AI applications such as custom GPTs for situation reporting, needs assessment, and public communication. The initiative builds on OpenAI's broader program to integrate AI into real-world operational challenges faced by disaster response teams, especially as Asia remains the world's most disaster-prone region with increasing climate-related emergencies.

items.title: STADLER integrates ChatGPT across 650 employees to accelerate knowledge work and improve productivity at its 230-year-old recycling technology company [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: STADLER reshapes knowledge work at a 230-year-old company
items.summary:
STADLER, a family-owned company with over 230 years of history specializing in automated waste sorting, has embedded ChatGPT into daily workflows for its 650 employees to enhance speed, quality, and decision-making. The company reports 30-40% time savings on common knowledge tasks and over 85% daily active usage since adopting the AI tool in 2023.

The rollout involved creating more than 125 custom GPTs tailored to various functions including engineering, project management, and marketing. Employees use ChatGPT for drafting, summarizing, translating, and structuring complex information, reducing the time to first draft by 2.5 times on average. Leadership combined bottom-up experimentation with top-down support to encourage widespread adoption and training.

STADLER plans to evolve AI use from assistance to execution by integrating AI agents into core workflows that can automate information gathering, output generation, validation, and approval routing. This transformation aims to increase organizational agility and unlock new productivity levels across its global operations.

items.title: OpenAI publishes Model Spec as a public framework to guide AI model behavior, balancing safety, user freedom, and accountability [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Inside our approach to the Model Spec
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced the Model Spec, a formal and publicly accessible framework that defines intended behaviors for its AI models to ensure fairness, safety, and user empowerment. The framework aims to make model behavior explicit and legible to users, developers, researchers, and policymakers, supporting transparency and iterative improvement.

The Model Spec complements OpenAI's broader safety initiatives by providing clear guidance on how models should respond across diverse queries, balancing goals such as harm prevention and operational licensing. Since its initial release in 2024, the Model Spec has evolved based on user feedback and expanding AI capabilities, serving as both an internal training and governance tool and an external reference for public scrutiny and input.

items.originalTitle: Introducing the OpenAI Safety Bug Bounty program
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced a public Safety Bug Bounty program aimed at detecting and addressing AI-specific safety and abuse risks across its products. The program targets vulnerabilities such as agentic behaviors, third-party prompt injection, data exfiltration, and account integrity issues that could lead to harm or misuse.

This initiative complements OpenAI's existing Security Bug Bounty by focusing on safety risks that do not qualify as traditional security vulnerabilities. Researchers can submit findings related to agentic risks, proprietary information leaks, and platform integrity, with submissions triaged by OpenAI's Safety and Security teams. The program excludes general content-policy bypasses and jailbreaks but may consider other user harm risks on a case-by-case basis.

items.summary:
The OpenAI Foundation announced it will invest a minimum of $1 billion over the next year to advance AI applications in life sciences, economic impact, AI resilience, and community support. The foundation aims to accelerate medical breakthroughs, improve economic opportunities, and prepare society for AI challenges.

Initial efforts focus on using AI to combat diseases like Alzheimer's, expanding public health data access, and supporting research on high-mortality diseases. The foundation is also engaging with experts to address AI's impact on jobs and the economy, while developing programs to enhance AI resilience and societal readiness.

These investments are part of a broader $25 billion commitment to curing diseases and AI resilience, with updates and new grants expected as the foundation scales its initiatives and refines its approach.

items.title: OpenAI details safety features in Sora 2 video generation model and app, including consent controls, content filtering, and protections for teens [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Creating with Sora Safely
items.summary:
OpenAI has outlined the safety measures integrated into its Sora 2 model and Sora app, designed to support secure video generation and social creation. These measures include visible and invisible provenance signals on generated videos, strict consent requirements for using real person likenesses, and enhanced guardrails for content involving minors and public figures. The platform also incorporates layered defenses against harmful content and audio misuse, along with user controls for sharing and reporting content.

The safety framework includes embedding industry-standard metadata, watermarking videos, and maintaining internal tools to trace content back to Sora. Teen users receive additional protections such as filtered feeds and parental controls. OpenAI emphasizes ongoing investment in audio safeguards and human review to address emerging risks. Users retain control over their content and can report or block abusive behavior, ensuring a balance between creative expression and user safety.

items.originalTitle: How we monitor internal coding agents for misalignment
items.summary:
OpenAI has developed an internal monitoring system using GPT-5.4 to observe and analyze the behavior of its coding agents, aiming to detect misalignment and security risks in real-world deployments. The system reviews agents' chains of thought and actions shortly after interactions, flagging behaviors that may conflict with user intent or internal policies to enable rapid mitigation and safeguard improvements.

This monitoring approach addresses unique risks posed by internal coding agents, which have access to sensitive systems and can modify safeguards. The system currently outperforms employee reports by identifying additional problematic behaviors and is evolving toward near real-time review to further enhance security. OpenAI has not found evidence of agents acting beyond their assigned tasks, and efforts continue to close monitoring gaps in bespoke or local setups.

items.summary:
OpenAI announced plans to acquire Astral, a developer of widely used open source Python tools such as uv, Ruff, and ty, to enhance its Codex AI platform. The acquisition aims to expand Codex's capabilities beyond code generation to support the full software development lifecycle, including planning, modifying, and maintaining code.

Astral's tools are integral to modern Python development, helping manage dependencies, enforce code quality, and improve type safety. OpenAI intends to continue supporting these open source projects while integrating them more deeply with Codex to enable AI agents to work seamlessly with developers' existing workflows. The acquisition is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approval.

items.originalTitle: Introducing GPT-5.4 mini and nano
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced GPT-5.4 mini and nano, smaller and faster versions of the GPT-5.4 model designed to improve performance in coding, reasoning, multimodal understanding, and tool use. These models target applications requiring low latency and cost efficiency, such as coding assistants, subagents handling simpler tasks, and real-time multimodal applications.

GPT-5.4 mini offers more than twice the speed of its predecessor GPT-5 mini while approaching the larger GPT-5.4's performance on benchmarks like SWE-Bench Pro and OSWorld-Verified. GPT-5.4 nano is the smallest and most cost-effective variant, recommended for classification, data extraction, ranking, and coding subagents. Both models are available through OpenAI's API, Codex, and ChatGPT platforms, with pricing scaled to their size and capabilities.

items.originalTitle: OpenAI Japan announces Japan Teen Safety Blueprint to put teen safety first
items.summary:
OpenAI Japan has launched the Japan Teen Safety Blueprint, a framework designed to improve safety for teenagers using generative AI by implementing advanced age-aware protections, stronger safety policies for users under 18, and expanded parental controls. The initiative aims to address risks such as exposure to misinformation, inappropriate content, and psychological strain while supporting teen well-being.

The blueprint includes privacy-conscious, risk-based age estimation with appeals processes, safeguards against harmful content and behaviors, and tools for families to manage usage and privacy settings. OpenAI is collaborating with clinicians, researchers, educators, and child safety experts to continuously improve features and research AI's impact on teen mental health. This effort builds on existing ChatGPT safeguards and aligns with Japan's approach to balancing protection and responsible technology access.

items.originalTitle: Equipping workers with insights about compensation
items.summary:
OpenAI reports that Americans use ChatGPT nearly 3 million times daily to obtain wage and compensation information, helping to address the difficulty workers face in accessing clear pay data. This usage is especially common among workers early in their careers, switching fields, or in roles where pay is less transparent or more negotiable.

The research highlights that ChatGPT users seek help translating pay into benchmarks and understanding realistic earnings for roles, companies, or entrepreneurial ventures, with queries concentrated in creative, management, healthcare, and technical fields. OpenAI's evaluation of GPT-5.4 shows high accuracy in estimating wages compared to official benchmarks, indicating AI's growing role as a labor market resource to support better career and compensation decisions.

items.title: OpenAI explains why Codex Security avoids traditional SAST reports, focusing on behavior validation and constraint reasoning to reduce false positives [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Why Codex Security Doesn’t Include a SAST Report
items.summary:
OpenAI's Codex Security deliberately does not use traditional static application security testing (SAST) reports, instead starting analysis directly from the code repository to understand architecture, trust boundaries, and intended behavior. This approach aims to validate security checks more accurately by reasoning about whether defenses truly constrain inputs after transformations, rather than just tracking data flow from source to sink.

The company highlights that conventional SAST struggles with approximations and cannot reliably determine if sanitizers or validations are sufficient given complex code behaviors like decoding and normalization. Codex Security uses AI-driven techniques to analyze the entire transformation chain and validate potential vulnerabilities in an isolated environment before surfacing them, reducing false positives and focusing on real security risks.

items.originalTitle: From model to agent: Equipping the Responses API with a computer environment
items.summary:
OpenAI has enhanced its Responses API by integrating it with a shell tool and hosted container workspaces, creating an agent runtime that can execute complex workflows within a secure computer environment. This setup allows models to interact with files, run commands, access APIs, and maintain state, expanding their capabilities beyond static task execution.

The system orchestrates a loop where the model proposes shell commands, which are executed in isolated containers with controlled filesystem and network access. Output is streamed back to the model in real time, enabling iterative decision-making and task completion. This approach addresses practical challenges like managing intermediate files, network security, and workflow reliability, aiming to simplify agent development and support more versatile, repeatable production workflows.

items.summary:

The AI-powered tool assists in incident response, automated code review, vulnerability checks, and supports more autonomous development across Rakuten's complex product ecosystem.

Codex is used to accelerate root-cause analysis and remediation through KQL-based monitoring, enforce internal coding standards in continuous integration and deployment pipelines, and execute larger projects from partial specifications. This approach allows Rakuten to maintain safety and reliability while significantly increasing development speed. The company is shifting engineers' roles toward defining clear specifications and verifying AI-generated outputs rather than manual code inspection.

This integration has enabled the company to correct 2.5 million product tags and automate 41,000 supplier support tickets monthly, improving operational efficiency and customer experience.

The company developed a reusable AI architecture using a single OpenAI model to classify product attributes at scale, replacing costly bespoke models. Wayfair also implemented a structured audit process to validate AI-driven catalog updates and collaborated with suppliers to ensure data quality. Additionally, AI-powered features in its supplier support tool Wilma have streamlined ticket routing and resolution, addressing the complexity of thousands of issue types.

items.title: OpenAI launches IH-Challenge training dataset to improve instruction hierarchy, safety steerability, and prompt injection robustness in frontier LLMs [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Improving instruction hierarchy in frontier LLMs
items.summary:
OpenAI introduced IH-Challenge, a reinforcement learning training dataset designed to help large language models prioritize instructions based on trust levels, enhancing their ability to follow safety policies and resist prompt injection attacks. This approach addresses conflicts between system, developer, user, and tool instructions by training models to respect a clear instruction hierarchy, which is crucial for safe and reliable AI behavior.

The IH-Challenge tasks are designed to be simple, objectively gradable, and resistant to shortcuts that could undermine training effectiveness. Models trained on IH-Challenge, such as the internal GPT-5 Mini-R, show improved performance on instruction hierarchy benchmarks and maintain overall usefulness without excessive refusals. This training method helps models generalize safety improvements to new and adversarial instruction conflicts, supporting safer AI deployment.

items.title: OpenAI launches interactive visual explanations for over 70 math and science concepts in ChatGPT to enhance learning globally [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: New ways to learn math and science in ChatGPT
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced interactive visual explanations in ChatGPT to help users better understand math and science concepts by manipulating variables and formulas in real time. This feature, available globally across all plans starting March 2026, aims to make abstract topics more accessible and improve conceptual understanding for students and learners.

The new tools cover more than 70 core topics relevant to high school and college learners, including the Pythagorean theorem, PV=nRT, and Ohm's law. Early feedback from students, parents, and educators indicates that these interactive modules support deeper learning beyond memorization by encouraging exploration and experimentation with concepts. OpenAI plans to expand these interactive learning features and continue research on AI's impact on education through initiatives like NextGenAI and the OpenAI Learning Lab.

items.summary:

The acquisition aims to integrate Promptfoo's automated security testing and evaluation tools directly into OpenAI Frontier, OpenAI's platform for building and managing AI agents.

The acquisition is subject to customary closing conditions, and OpenAI intends to continue developing both the open-source project and enhanced enterprise capabilities within Frontier to help organizations deploy secure and reliable AI systems.

items.title: OpenAI launches Codex Security in research preview to identify and fix complex software vulnerabilities with improved accuracy and reduced false positives [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Codex Security: now in research preview
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Codex Security, an AI-driven application security tool now available in research preview for ChatGPT Pro, Enterprise, Business, and Edu customers. The tool builds deep context about software projects to detect complex vulnerabilities, prioritize findings by real-world impact, validate issues in sandboxed environments, and propose patches that align with system intent, aiming to reduce noise and accelerate secure code deployment.

Codex Security, formerly known as Aardvark, began as a private beta and has demonstrated significant improvements in detection precision, cutting false positives by over 50% and reducing over-reported severity by more than 90%. It scanned over 1.2 million commits in the last 30 days, identifying hundreds of critical and high-severity issues while minimizing unnecessary triage for security teams. The system also learns from user feedback to refine its threat models and improve future findings.

items.title: Descript uses OpenAI reasoning models to scale multilingual video dubbing with improved timing and semantic fidelity [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: How Descript engineers multilingual video dubbing at scale
items.summary:
Descript has developed a multilingual video dubbing system that leverages OpenAI's GPT-5 reasoning models to automatically localize large video libraries while preserving original timing and meaning. This approach addresses challenges in duration adherence across languages, enabling more natural dubbed audio without manual retiming or rewriting.

The system breaks transcripts into chunks and optimizes translations for both semantic fidelity and duration constraints during generation, rather than correcting timing afterward. Since rollout, Descript reported a 15% increase in dubbed video exports and a 13 to 43 percentage point improvement in duration adherence, depending on the language. This advancement supports scalable dubbing for enterprise localization projects and improves user experience by avoiding unnatural speech pacing in dubbed content.

items.title: OpenAI finds reasoning models struggle to control their chains of thought, supporting chain-of-thought monitoring as an AI safety measure [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Reasoning models struggle to control their chains of thought, and that’s good
items.summary: OpenAI introduced CoT-Control, an evaluation suite to measure reasoning models' ability to control their chains of thought (CoT) under user instructions. Their study across 13 frontier models found low CoT controllability, with compliance rates below 15.4%, indicating models often fail to deliberately alter or obscure their reasoning even when aware of monitoring. This limitation suggests that current models remain interpretable and monitorable, reinforcing the effectiveness of CoT monitoring as a safeguard in AI development. The research highlights the importance of ongoing evaluation as AI capabilities evolve to ensure monitoring remains reliable and effective.

items.originalTitle: Introducing ChatGPT for Excel and new financial data integrations
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT for Excel in beta, embedding its GPT-5.4 model directly into spreadsheets to help users build, update, and analyze models faster. The tool supports financial workflows by enabling scenario analysis, error tracing, and formula explanations within Excel workbooks, aiming to reduce manual work and improve consistency across teams.

Alongside ChatGPT for Excel, OpenAI has added financial data integrations with providers like FactSet, Dow Jones Factiva, LSEG, Daloopa, and S&P Global, allowing users to access trusted market and company data within ChatGPT. These features target finance professionals by streamlining data extraction, modeling, and research tasks that typically require significant time and effort.

ChatGPT for Excel is available globally to various ChatGPT subscription tiers, with enterprise and educational users able to enable access via admin controls. OpenAI continues to refine the tool based on user feedback, acknowledging some limitations in formula complexity and response times during the beta phase.

This approach reduced reliance on external agencies and addressed challenges like repetitive tasks and knowledge bottlenecks. VfL Wolfsburg plans to expand AI capabilities further, including fan- and partner-facing applications, as governance and accountability structures mature.

items.title: OpenAI researchers use GPT-5.2 Pro to extend single-minus amplitude results to gravitons, revealing nonzero tree-level graviton interactions under special kinematic conditions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Extending single-minus amplitudes to gravitons
items.summary:
Researchers from OpenAI and academic institutions published a preprint demonstrating that single-minus graviton tree amplitudes, previously assumed to vanish, can be nonzero in a half-collinear momentum regime. The study extends earlier gluon amplitude results to quantum gravity, showing these amplitudes arise as well-defined mathematical distributions supported on restricted momentum configurations. GPT-5.2 Pro assisted in deriving and verifying the new formulas, employing recursion relations and symmetry principles.

The work highlights an infinite-dimensional symmetry related to Penrose's w-(1+∞) algebra acting on gravitons, which may be important for quantizing gravity. The derivation was checked analytically and found consistent with known physical limits and symmetry constraints. This project illustrates how AI tools can accelerate complex theoretical physics research by aiding in conjecture generation and formal write-up preparation.

items.originalTitle: How Axios uses AI to help deliver high-impact local journalism
items.summary:
Axios integrates AI across its local journalism workflow to help reporters produce clearer, sharper stories faster, allowing a single reporter to cover more communities effectively. The company uses a custom GPT tool called the Axiomizer to refine headlines and summaries, freeing journalists to focus on reporting rather than editing and formatting tasks.

This AI-driven approach addresses economic challenges in local news by reducing production costs and enabling coverage in smaller markets with fewer staff. AI also helps reporters quickly analyze public data like government meetings, making previously inaccessible information usable for impactful local stories. Axios emphasizes that human reporters remain central to maintaining community trust and voice while AI supports operational efficiency.

items.title: OpenAI launches Learning Outcomes Measurement Suite to assess AI's long-term impact on student learning across diverse educational settings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Understanding AI and learning outcomes
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced the Learning Outcomes Measurement Suite, a framework developed with the University of Tartu and Stanford's SCALE Initiative to evaluate how AI tools affect student learning over time in various educational contexts. This initiative aims to move beyond traditional test score metrics to capture the broader influence of AI on learning processes.

The suite is currently undergoing validation through a randomized controlled trial involving over 300 college students and is part of OpenAI's Learning Lab research ecosystem, which includes partners like Arizona State University, UCL Knowledge Lab, and MIT Media Lab. OpenAI plans to publish ongoing research findings and eventually make the measurement suite publicly available to support educators and institutions worldwide in understanding AI's role in education.

items.originalTitle: OpenAI and Amazon announce strategic partnership
items.summary:
OpenAI and Amazon have formed a multi-year strategic partnership in which Amazon will invest $50 billion in OpenAI and serve as the exclusive third-party cloud provider for OpenAI Frontier. They will co-develop a Stateful Runtime Environment powered by OpenAI models, available through Amazon Bedrock, to help enterprises build and deploy AI applications and agents at scale.

OpenAI will consume approximately 2 gigawatts of AWS Trainium capacity to support this collaboration, including future Trainium4 chips expected in 2027. The partnership also includes developing customized AI models for Amazon's customer-facing applications, aiming to integrate advanced AI capabilities seamlessly into AWS infrastructure and Amazon's products.

The funding supports expanded AI compute capacity, distribution, and capital to meet growing demand from consumers, developers, and businesses worldwide.

The company has also formed strategic partnerships with Amazon and NVIDIA to enhance global reach and infrastructure, including dedicated inference and training capacity. OpenAI's products like Codex and ChatGPT have seen significant user growth, with over 900 million weekly active users and more than 50 million consumer subscribers, reflecting increased adoption across individual and enterprise use cases.

This funding round strengthens the OpenAI Foundation's stake and philanthropic capacity, enabling further investment in health breakthroughs and AI resilience. OpenAI aims to accelerate AI innovation and deployment at scale, emphasizing collaboration with key partners to deliver reliable and broadly useful AI systems.

items.title: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and OpenAI develop DraftNEPABench to evaluate AI agents accelerating federal infrastructure permitting, showing up to 15% drafting time reduction [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and OpenAI partner to accelerate federal permitting
items.summary:
Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and OpenAI have partnered to create DraftNEPABench, a benchmark designed to assess AI coding agents' effectiveness in speeding up the drafting of National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) documents. Initial evaluations with 19 experts indicate that AI could reduce drafting time by up to 15%, potentially modernizing the federal permitting process for infrastructure projects.

The collaboration involved testing AI models on tasks related to NEPA workflows across documents from 18 federal agencies, focusing on reading, synthesizing, verifying, and drafting complex regulatory content. This effort aims to help federal agencies review and approve infrastructure proposals more efficiently while maintaining accuracy and compliance with legal standards.

By integrating AI tools like Codex CLI and GPT-5, the project explores how coding agents can assist government workers by handling time-consuming drafting tasks, allowing human reviewers to focus on oversight and complex decision-making. The benchmark highlights both the potential and current limitations of AI in supporting federal permitting workflows.

items.originalTitle: OpenAI Codex and Figma launch seamless code-to-design experience
items.summary:
OpenAI and Figma have introduced a new integration that connects OpenAI's Codex directly to Figma's design platform, enabling users to move smoothly between coding and design. This integration allows teams to generate Figma designs from code and convert Figma files back into code, facilitating faster iteration and product development.

The integration uses Figma's MCP Server, an open-source standard that links AI agents with external tools, to support workflows across Figma Design, Figma Make, and FigJam. It builds on the existing partnership between OpenAI and Figma, which includes the Figma app in ChatGPT and the use of OpenAI models across Figma's platform. This new capability aims to reduce barriers between design and engineering roles by enabling continuous translation between design intent and implementation.

items.title: OpenAI stops reporting SWE-bench Verified scores due to contamination and flawed tests, recommends SWE-bench Pro for reliable software engineering model evaluation [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Why we no longer evaluate SWE-bench Verified
items.summary:
OpenAI has ceased using SWE-bench Verified to measure autonomous software engineering capabilities because the benchmark is contaminated and contains flawed test cases that reject correct solutions. Analysis showed that many models had seen the benchmark problems and solutions during training, leading to inflated performance that does not reflect real-world coding ability.

SWE-bench Verified was created in 2024 to improve on the original SWE-bench by filtering problematic tasks, but recent findings revealed that over half of audited problems had faulty tests and that training data leakage compromised the benchmark's validity. OpenAI is developing new uncontaminated evaluations and advises the research community to use SWE-bench Pro until better metrics are available.

items.originalTitle: Our First Proof submissions
items.summary:
OpenAI has released its first AI-generated proof attempts for the First Proof challenge, a research-level math test requiring complex, checkable proofs in specialized domains. The AI model tackled all 10 problems, with experts indicating that at least five of the proofs have a high chance of correctness, while others remain under review or were found incorrect after further analysis.

The model was trained with limited human supervision and improved over time, solving increasingly difficult problems. OpenAI used expert feedback and iterative prompting to refine proofs and collaborated with ChatGPT for verification and formatting. This effort builds on prior AI research achievements in mathematics and science, and OpenAI plans to engage further with the community to develop more rigorous evaluation methods and enhance future models' reasoning capabilities.

items.title: OpenAI commits $7.5 million to The Alignment Project to fund independent AI alignment research addressing safety and security risks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Advancing independent research on AI alignment
items.summary:
OpenAI has pledged $7.5 million to The Alignment Project, a global fund managed by the UK AI Security Institute, to support independent research focused on mitigating safety and security risks from misaligned artificial intelligence. This funding aims to strengthen the broader ecosystem of alignment research beyond frontier labs as AI systems become more capable and autonomous.

The grant contributes to a total fund exceeding £27 million, which supports diverse projects worldwide in areas such as computational complexity, economic theory, cognitive science, and cryptography. The Alignment Project, backed by public, philanthropic, and industry partners, funds vetted research proposals and offers optional compute resources and expert support to advance foundational and exploratory AI safety work.

items.title: OpenAI and Paradigm launch EVMbench to benchmark AI agents' detection, patching, and exploitation of smart contract vulnerabilities [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing EVMbench
items.summary:
OpenAI and Paradigm have introduced EVMbench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents' abilities to detect, patch, and exploit critical vulnerabilities in smart contracts securing over $100 billion in crypto assets. The benchmark includes 117 curated vulnerabilities from 40 audits and scenarios from the Tempo blockchain, focusing on payment-oriented smart contract code.

EVMbench tests AI agents in three modes: detecting vulnerabilities, patching contracts without breaking functionality, and exploiting contracts in a sandboxed environment. The benchmark uses a Rust-based harness for reproducible evaluation and has revealed that agents perform best in exploitation tasks but face challenges in exhaustive detection and effective patching. While EVMbench reflects realistic vulnerabilities, it does not capture the full complexity of real-world smart contract security and has some grading limitations.

items.title: OpenAI's GPT-5.2 proposes and helps prove a new formula for gluon scattering amplitudes in theoretical physics [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: GPT-5.2 derives a new result in theoretical physics
items.summary:
OpenAI's GPT-5.2 generated a novel formula for a specific gluon scattering amplitude previously assumed to be zero, which was then formally proven and verified by researchers from OpenAI and academic institutions. The work challenges standard assumptions about particle interactions under special momentum alignments known as the half-collinear regime.

The preprint, coauthored by physicists from the Institute for Advanced Study, Vanderbilt University, University of Cambridge, Harvard University, and OpenAI, details how GPT-5.2 simplified complex expressions and conjectured a general formula for all particle counts. An internal version of GPT-5.2 then produced a formal proof, which was validated against established physics recursion relations and the soft theorem. This AI-assisted approach has also been extended to graviton amplitudes, with further generalizations underway.
