items.title: OpenAI launches Lockdown Mode and Elevated Risk labels in ChatGPT to enhance security against prompt injection and data exfiltration [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing Lockdown Mode and Elevated Risk labels in ChatGPT
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Lockdown Mode and Elevated Risk labels in ChatGPT to provide stronger protections against prompt injection attacks and AI-driven data exfiltration. Lockdown Mode is an optional security setting that restricts ChatGPT's access to external services and web features, aimed at users with higher security needs such as executives and security teams.

Lockdown Mode limits or disables features like live web access, image support, and file downloads to reduce the risk of sensitive information being leaked. It is currently available for ChatGPT Enterprise, Edu, Healthcare, and Teachers plans, with plans to roll out to personal accounts. Elevated Risk labels highlight capabilities that may introduce additional security risks, helping users and organizations make informed decisions about AI usage.

items.title: OpenAI launches GABRIEL, an open-source GPT-based toolkit to convert qualitative text and images into quantitative data for social science research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Scaling social science research
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced GABRIEL, an open-source Python library designed to help economists, social scientists, and data scientists analyze qualitative data at scale by turning unstructured text and images into measurable quantitative scores. The tool allows researchers to specify measurement criteria in natural language and apply them consistently across large datasets, reducing the time spent on manual data labeling.

GABRIEL supports various research tasks such as analyzing scientific papers, course curricula, historical records, and customer reviews, while also offering features like dataset merging, deduplication, passage coding, theory ideation, and text deidentification to protect privacy. OpenAI plans to improve GABRIEL based on academic feedback to make qualitative data more accessible for rigorous social science analysis.

items.title: OpenAI details harness engineering approach using Codex to build a million lines of code with no manual coding over five months [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
items.summary:
OpenAI's technical staff member Ryan Lopopolo describes an experiment where a software product was developed entirely by Codex agents without any manually written code, resulting in about a million lines of code over five months. The team focused on designing environments and feedback loops to enable Codex to execute tasks, shifting the engineers' role from coding to steering and specifying intent.

The project began with an empty repository and used GPT-5 guided Codex to generate all initial scaffolding and code. Over 1,500 pull requests were merged by a small team, with agent-to-agent code review processes reducing human review needs. The approach increased engineering velocity significantly, highlighting new challenges in making applications legible to AI agents and managing human attention as the main bottleneck.

The deployment supports unclassified work with built-in safety controls and runs on authorized government cloud infrastructure to protect sensitive data.

The ChatGPT system is designed to assist with tasks such as summarizing policy documents, drafting procurement materials, generating reports, and supporting research and mission workflows. Data processed on GenAI.mil remains isolated from OpenAI’s public models to ensure security and compliance with government standards.

items.title: OpenAI outlines its approach to localizing AI for diverse languages, laws, and cultures through the OpenAI for Countries initiative [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Making AI work for everyone, everywhere: our approach to localization
items.summary:
OpenAI has detailed its strategy for adapting AI technologies to local languages, legal frameworks, and cultural contexts worldwide to ensure AI benefits all populations safely and effectively. The company emphasizes the importance of sovereign AI systems tailored to specific countries rather than simple translations, aiming to meet local needs while maintaining global model standards.

As part of this effort, OpenAI is piloting a localized version of ChatGPT for Estonian students that incorporates local curricula and teaching methods. The company’s Model Spec sets binding rules for AI behavior globally, including prohibitions on enabling severe harms and commitments to transparency, privacy, and human rights. OpenAI plans to continue sharing insights and evolving its localization approach through the OpenAI for Countries program.

items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Trusted Access for Cyber, a framework designed to ensure that advanced cybersecurity capabilities powered by its GPT-5.3-Codex model are accessible only to verified users focused on defense. This initiative aims to accelerate vulnerability discovery and remediation while reducing the risk of misuse by requiring identity verification and trust-based access controls.

The program includes automated monitoring to detect suspicious activity and an invite-only option for security researchers needing more permissive access. OpenAI is also committing $10 million in API credits through its Cybersecurity Grant Program to support teams with proven records in identifying and fixing vulnerabilities in open source and critical infrastructure software. The approach balances expanding access to frontier cyber tools with safeguards to prevent malicious use and will evolve based on early participant feedback.

items.originalTitle: Introducing OpenAI Frontier
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Frontier, a new enterprise platform designed to facilitate the building, deployment, and management of AI agents that can perform real work across organizations. The platform provides features such as shared context, onboarding processes, hands-on learning with feedback, and clear permissions and boundaries to enable AI coworkers to operate effectively alongside human teams.

Frontier integrates with existing enterprise systems across multiple clouds without requiring replatforming, supporting open standards and allowing AI agents to work through various interfaces. Early adopters include HP, Intuit, Oracle, State Farm, Thermo Fisher, and Uber, with other companies piloting the platform to enhance complex AI workflows and improve operational efficiency.

items.summary:
OpenAI has launched GPT-5.3-Codex, its most capable agentic coding model to date, which integrates advanced coding performance from GPT-5.2-Codex with enhanced reasoning and professional knowledge from GPT-5.2. This model supports complex, long-running tasks involving research, tool use, and execution, allowing interactive steering without losing context.

GPT-5.3-Codex is treated as high capability in biology and cybersecurity domains, with OpenAI implementing corresponding safeguards under its Preparedness Framework. While it does not reach high capability in AI self-improvement, the cybersecurity safeguards aim to prevent misuse while enabling defensive applications.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-5.3-Codex, a faster agentic coding model with enhanced reasoning and professional knowledge capabilities [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing GPT-5.3-Codex
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced GPT-5.3-Codex, an advanced coding model that combines improved coding performance with general reasoning and professional knowledge, enabling it to handle complex, long-term technical tasks. The model is 25% faster than its predecessor and can maintain context during extended interactions, supporting a wide range of software development activities beyond coding, including debugging, deployment, and user research.

GPT-5.3-Codex achieved state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks such as SWE-Bench Pro and Terminal-Bench 2.0, demonstrating superior coding and terminal skills across multiple programming languages. It also excels in web development, autonomously iterating on complex projects like games over millions of tokens. The model better understands user intent for everyday web tasks, producing more functional and polished outputs by default.

Beyond software engineering, GPT-5.3-Codex supports various professional knowledge work tasks, matching previous models on evaluations across 44 occupations. OpenAI used early versions of GPT-5.3-Codex to assist in its own development process, highlighting its agentic capabilities and potential to perform diverse computer-based professional tasks.

items.title: OpenAI details development of Codex App Server using bidirectional JSON-RPC API to unify Codex agent across multiple platforms [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Unlocking the Codex harness: how we built the App Server
items.summary:
OpenAI explains how it built the Codex App Server to serve as a client-friendly, bidirectional JSON-RPC API that powers the Codex coding agent across various interfaces including web, CLI, IDE extensions, and a macOS app. The server enables features like streaming progress updates, tool execution, approval workflows, and difference tracking, allowing consistent agent behavior across products.

The App Server originated to reuse the Codex harness across different products without re-implementing core logic, evolving from a terminal user interface to a stable platform supporting multiple clients such as JetBrains, Xcode, and the Codex desktop app. It manages thread lifecycle, configuration, authentication, and tool execution within a long-lived process that hosts Codex core threads, facilitating rich interactions and backward-compatible integration for partners and internal teams.

This architecture allows developers to embed Codex capabilities into their products to enhance software development workflows, supporting use cases like code review, site reliability engineering, and coding assistance through a consistent and extensible protocol.

items.title: OpenAI outlines Sora feed philosophy prioritizing creativity, user control, connection, and safety with personalized recommendations and parental controls [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: The Sora feed philosophy
items.summary:
OpenAI's Sora feed philosophy aims to inspire creativity and foster connections by optimizing for active participation and allowing users to steer content ranking. The feed includes personalized recommendations based on user activity, ChatGPT data, and engagement signals, with parental controls to manage personalization and continuous scrolling for teens.

The system balances safety and freedom by implementing robust guardrails to prevent harmful content, filtering age-inappropriate material, and enforcing global usage policies. Content violating these policies, such as graphic violence, extremist propaganda, or bullying, is removed through automated tools and human review to maintain a safe and expressive environment for all users.

items.title: OpenAI and Snowflake announce $200 million partnership to integrate advanced AI models into Snowflake's enterprise data platform [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Snowflake and OpenAI partner to bring frontier intelligence to enterprise data
items.summary:
OpenAI and Snowflake have formed a multi-year, $200 million partnership to embed OpenAI's advanced AI models, including GPT-5.2, directly into Snowflake's data platform. This integration allows Snowflake customers to build AI agents and generate insights from their enterprise data using tools like Snowflake Cortex AI and Snowflake Intelligence without coding.

The collaboration aims to accelerate AI adoption across industries by enabling natural-language queries and multimodal data analysis within Snowflake's secure and governed environment. Customers such as Canva and WHOOP have highlighted the partnership's role in enhancing data-driven decision-making and AI-powered applications while maintaining enterprise security and compliance standards.

items.title: OpenAI launches Codex app for macOS as a command center to manage multiple AI coding agents and support parallel workflows [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing the Codex app
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced the Codex app for macOS, designed as a command center to help developers manage multiple AI agents simultaneously, run parallel tasks, and collaborate on long-running software projects. The app supports isolated worktrees to prevent code conflicts and integrates with existing Codex tools like the CLI and IDE extensions to streamline development workflows.

The Codex app extends beyond code generation by incorporating skills that enable agents to perform complex tasks such as information gathering, problem-solving, and workflow automation. OpenAI demonstrated the app's capabilities by having Codex independently develop a 3D voxel kart racing game using multiple skills and millions of tokens from a single user prompt. The app is now also available on Windows, and OpenAI has increased Codex usage limits across various subscription plans to encourage broader adoption.

The agent supports natural language queries, automates complex data exploration, and improves over time through self-learning memory.

The agent integrates with tools like Slack, IDEs, and OpenAI's internal ChatGPT app, enabling teams across Engineering, Data Science, Finance, and Research to access insights in minutes rather than days. It handles the full analytics workflow from data discovery to report generation, reducing the need for manual SQL debugging and allowing users to focus on decision-making.

items.title: OpenAI to retire GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, and o4-mini models from ChatGPT on February 13, 2026, following earlier GPT-5 retirements [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Retiring GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, and OpenAI o4-mini in ChatGPT
items.summary:
OpenAI announced it will retire several older GPT-4 models, including GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, and OpenAI o4-mini, from the ChatGPT platform on February 13, 2026. This move coincides with the previously planned discontinuation of GPT-5 variants but does not affect the API at this time.

The decision follows user feedback favoring GPT-4o's conversational style and warmth, which influenced improvements in GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2, including enhanced personality and creative ideation features. OpenAI noted that the vast majority of users have shifted to GPT-5.2, with only 0.1% still using GPT-4o daily.

OpenAI plans to continue refining ChatGPT's personality, creativity, and response behavior, aiming to offer more user control and customization while maintaining appropriate safeguards, including age prediction features for users under 18 in most markets.

items.title: Taisei Corporation rolls out ChatGPT Enterprise to enhance talent development and AI adoption across its workforce [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Taisei Corporation shapes the next generation of talent with AI
items.summary:
Taisei Corporation, a leading Japanese construction company, has implemented ChatGPT Enterprise through its Human Resources team to support AI-powered talent development and expand employee potential. The rollout focuses on integrating AI into daily work to foster learning and growth rather than just improving efficiency.

The company adopted a "Middle Out" approach combining leadership direction with frontline engagement, creating training programs and communities to encourage practical AI use. Taisei also prioritized safety and trust by implementing access controls, usage monitoring, and education, resulting in high adoption rates, significant time savings per employee, and thousands of custom GPTs created. The company aims to embed AI use into its culture and share its human-centered AI model with the broader construction industry.

items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced the EMEA Youth & Wellbeing Grant, a €500,000 funding program aimed at supporting NGOs and research organizations working to improve youth safety, wellbeing, and development in the context of artificial intelligence across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. The grant targets projects that produce practical tools, independent research, or initiatives that help young people benefit safely from AI.

The program offers grants typically ranging from €25,000 to €100,000, with multi-year awards possible for larger efforts. Eligible applicants must be operational NGOs or research institutions registered in the EMEA region, focusing on youth safety or AI impacts on minors. Applications for 2026 have closed, and finalists have been selected, with projects expected to begin in the second or third quarter of 2026.

items.originalTitle: The next chapter for AI in the EU
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced the EU Economic Blueprint 2.0, featuring updated data on AI usage in Europe and initiatives to accelerate AI adoption among individuals, businesses, and governments. The plan includes a program to train 20,000 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in AI skills, supported by Booking.com, and a €500,000 grant to support research on youth safety and wellbeing in the digital age.

The Blueprint highlights disparities in AI usage across EU member states and emphasizes the need for national AI strategies, education frameworks, and skills accreditation to close the capability gap. OpenAI also plans to expand partnerships with European governments through its OpenAI for Europe initiative, focusing on education, health, and AI skills training to support national AI priorities.

items.title: OpenAI implements safeguards to prevent data leaks when AI agents fetch URLs by verifying links against a public web index [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Keeping your data safe when an AI agent clicks a link
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced measures to protect user data when AI agents interact with web links, addressing risks of data exfiltration through URLs and prompt injection attacks. The system checks whether a URL has been previously observed on the public web before allowing automatic fetching, reducing the chance of leaking private information.

This approach avoids relying solely on trusted site lists, which can be bypassed through redirects or cause user friction. When a URL is unverified, users receive warnings and must explicitly approve access, maintaining control over potentially sensitive data exposure. These safeguards focus on preventing quiet data leaks via URLs but do not guarantee the trustworthiness of web content or protection against social engineering.

Indeed balances rapid AI innovation with responsible use, ensuring employers remain the final decision-makers. Recent AI launches include Career Scout, a personal career coach for job seekers, and Talent Scout, which automates recruiting tasks for employers. Internally, AI adoption has freed employees from repetitive work, enabling more strategic efforts, with over 80% of engineers using AI tools and many employees saving up to two hours weekly.

To build AI fluency, Indeed offers company-wide training and encourages bottom-up sharing of AI use cases, fostering a culture of curiosity and continuous learning. The company also hosts internal hackathons and contests to promote practical and engaging AI adoption across teams.

items.title: OpenAI scales PostgreSQL to support 800 million ChatGPT users with millions of queries per second through replicas, caching, and workload isolation [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Scaling PostgreSQL to power 800 million ChatGPT users
items.summary:
OpenAI has scaled its PostgreSQL database infrastructure to handle the demands of approximately 800 million ChatGPT users by implementing extensive optimizations including read replicas, caching layers, rate limiting, and workload isolation. This approach allows a single primary PostgreSQL instance, supported by nearly 50 read replicas across multiple regions, to manage millions of queries per second despite rapid traffic growth.

The company addressed challenges related to PostgreSQL's multiversion concurrency control (MVCC) and write amplification by migrating write-heavy workloads to sharded systems like Azure Cosmos DB, while maintaining a single-primary architecture for read-heavy workloads. These engineering efforts have enabled PostgreSQL to reliably support massive global traffic with ongoing improvements to prevent overloads and outages.

items.summary:

These agents adapt lessons in real time based on learner behavior, progress, and conversation context to help users build practical fluency in real-world situations. The system includes a Lesson Agent that conducts conversations, a Student Progress Agent that monitors language performance, and a Learning Planning Agent that adjusts long-term learning goals, all supported by a memory layer that ensures responses are contextually relevant and timely.

The app addresses common gaps in traditional language education by focusing on conversational practice and real-time adaptation, using advanced speech recognition to handle non-native and imperfect speech. This approach has led to measurable improvements, including a 24% increase in day-one retention and doubled revenue growth from the multi-agent system. Praktika’s founders, who have personal experience with language learning challenges, designed the platform to help learners gain confidence and fluency for work, study, and daily life.

items.originalTitle: Inside GPT-5 for Work: How Businesses Use GPT-5
items.summary:
OpenAI released a report analyzing how GPT-5 is being used by workers across various industries and departments, showing rapid adoption since its launch and diverse applications in writing, research, programming, and analysis. The report combines OpenAI's anonymized usage data with independent studies to provide insights into who is using GPT-5 at work and how it integrates into daily workflows.

The data reveals that sectors like IT and finance lead in GPT-5 adoption due to their information-heavy tasks, while industries such as retail and construction show slower uptake. Healthcare adoption is growing cautiously, influenced by privacy and compliance concerns. The report also notes that younger workers and knowledge-intensive roles are primary drivers of GPT-5 integration, signaling a shift toward mainstream AI use in enterprise settings.

items.originalTitle: How Higgsfield turns simple ideas into cinematic social videos
items.summary:
Higgsfield is a generative media platform that transforms simple ideas, product links, or images into short-form cinematic videos using OpenAI's GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 for planning and Sora 2 for video creation. The system produces about 4 million videos per day, enabling solo creators to achieve polished, social-first content efficiently.

The platform interprets user intent through a cinematic logic layer that converts creative goals into structured video plans, applying viral content patterns identified by AI analysis. Features like Click-to-Ad allow users to generate trend-aligned videos from product pages quickly, reducing the need for multiple iterations and supporting high-volume campaign production.

items.title: OpenAI outlines global AI adoption gaps and expands OpenAI for Countries initiative to boost AI integration in education, health, and public services in 2026 [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: How countries can end the capability overhang
items.summary:
OpenAI's new report reveals significant disparities in advanced AI usage across more than 70 countries, with some nations using three times more complex AI capabilities per person than others, regardless of income levels. The company highlights a growing capability overhang that risks widening economic and technological divides globally.

To address this, OpenAI is expanding its OpenAI for Countries program in 2026 with initiatives focused on education, health, AI skills training, disaster response, cybersecurity, and startup support. The program partners with governments to integrate AI into education systems and public services, aiming to improve productivity, innovation, and economic growth while tailoring approaches to local needs and capacities.

items.title: OpenAI launches Education for Countries initiative to help governments integrate AI into education systems and workforce training [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing Edu for Countries
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Education for Countries, a program designed to assist governments and universities in embedding AI tools into education systems to personalize learning, reduce administrative burdens, and prepare students for future workforce demands. The initiative includes access to AI models like ChatGPT Edu, research collaborations on AI's impact on learning, tailored training and certifications, and a global network of partners.

The first cohort includes Estonia, Greece, Italy, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Slovakia, Trinidad & Tobago, and the UAE, with Estonia already deploying AI tools nationwide in schools and universities. The program emphasizes phased rollouts, starting with educator training and pilot programs for students, alongside efforts to ensure AI safety and literacy for young users. This initiative aligns with OpenAI's mission to expand economic opportunity and ensure AI benefits everyone by supporting education and workforce readiness globally.

items.summary:
OpenAI and the Gates Foundation have announced Horizon 1000, a $50 million initiative aimed at enhancing AI capabilities in primary healthcare across Africa. The program plans to support 1,000 clinics and their communities by 2028, starting with Rwanda, to improve healthcare delivery and address workforce shortages.

The initiative will provide funding, technology, and technical support to African health leaders to deploy AI tools that assist frontline health workers with complex guidelines and reduce administrative burdens. This effort seeks to improve care quality and accessibility in regions facing significant health workforce deficits and variable care standards.

items.title: OpenAI develops Stargate Community plans to tailor AI infrastructure projects to local needs, focusing on energy, workforce, and community partnerships [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Stargate Community
items.summary:
OpenAI is advancing its Stargate AI infrastructure initiative with community-specific plans that prioritize local input, energy solutions, and workforce considerations to support economic growth and minimize impact. The program aims to expand U.S. AI capacity to 10GW by 2029, with sites already active or in development across Texas, New Mexico, Wisconsin, and Michigan.

Each Stargate site will implement a customized community plan that includes commitments to fund energy needs without raising local electricity prices, collaborating with utilities and regulators, and adopting flexible load management to support grid stability. Examples include partnerships with Oracle, Vantage, and local energy providers to develop renewable energy and storage solutions tailored to each region.

OpenAI also emphasizes environmental responsibility by minimizing water use through advanced cooling technologies and aims to be a good neighbor by contributing to local economies and infrastructure. The company highlights alignment with partners like Microsoft, which share community-first AI commitments for campus development.

items.title: OpenAI plans to test ads in ChatGPT's free and Go tiers in the US to expand affordable AI access while preserving user privacy and response quality [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Our approach to advertising and expanding access to ChatGPT
items.summary:
OpenAI announced plans to introduce advertising in the free and ChatGPT Go subscription tiers in the United States as part of its strategy to make AI technology more accessible globally. The company emphasized that ads will be clearly labeled, separate from ChatGPT's responses, and will not influence the answers provided. User data and conversations will remain private and will not be sold to advertisers.

The ad tests will begin in the coming weeks for logged-in adults in the US, with ads appearing at the bottom of answers when relevant to the conversation. OpenAI will exclude ads from accounts of users under 18 and from sensitive topics such as health and politics. The company also highlighted principles guiding its approach, including mission alignment, answer independence, conversation privacy, user control over data, and prioritizing user trust over revenue. Paid tiers like Pro, Business, and Enterprise will remain ad-free.

OpenAI has issued a new Request for Proposals aimed at strengthening the U.S. artificial intelligence supply chain by accelerating domestic manufacturing of key AI infrastructure components. The initiative targets manufacturing capacity for data center inputs, consumer electronics, and robotics to support AI ecosystem growth and resilience.

The RFP seeks proposals from manufacturers and suppliers prepared to build critical parts such as modules, tooling, assembly equipment, compute hardware, cooling systems, and power electronics within the United States. This effort builds on OpenAI's ongoing investments in AI infrastructure and aims to catalyze job creation, modernize supply chains, and reinforce American leadership in AI technology. Responses will inform future partnerships and procurement strategies, with a submission deadline set for June 2026.

The partnership combines OpenAI's data center engineering expertise with SB Energy's infrastructure and energy development capabilities to build optimized AI data centers expected to enter service starting in 2026.

The Milam County facility is designed to minimize water usage and will create thousands of construction jobs, with plans to support local energy needs and protect ratepayers. The collaboration also focuses on community investment through workforce development and grid modernization to foster economic growth in partner regions.

items.title: Datadog integrates OpenAI Codex for system-level code review to identify risks beyond traditional tools [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Datadog uses Codex for system-level code review
items.summary:
Datadog has integrated OpenAI's Codex into its code review process to bring system-wide context and improve detection of risks that traditional static analysis tools miss. This AI-assisted review helps engineers understand how code changes affect interconnected systems, aiming to prevent incidents and enhance reliability before production deployment.

The company piloted Codex by automatically reviewing pull requests in a major repository, with engineers providing positive feedback on the quality of suggestions. Codex was validated against historical incidents, identifying risks in about 22% of cases that human reviewers had overlooked. It highlights issues such as cross-service interactions, missing test coverage, and API contract changes, offering feedback that engineers consider valuable and comparable to senior human reviewers.

Datadog has since expanded Codex usage to over 1,000 engineers, who report that it helps them focus more on design and systemic risks rather than just surface-level code issues. The integration aims to complement human judgment and improve overall software reliability at scale.

OpenAI introduced OpenAI for Healthcare, a suite of secure AI tools designed to help healthcare organizations deliver consistent, high-quality care while complying with HIPAA regulations. The offering includes ChatGPT for Healthcare, which is already being adopted by major institutions such as AdventHealth and Stanford Medicine Children’s Health, and an API used by thousands of organizations for HIPAA-compliant applications.

ChatGPT for Healthcare features GPT-5 models tailored for clinical, research, and operational tasks, providing evidence-based responses with transparent citations from peer-reviewed sources. It integrates with enterprise systems to align with institutional policies and offers reusable templates to automate documentation workflows. The platform includes role-based access controls, data residency options, and a Business Associate Agreement to ensure patient data privacy and compliance, aiming to reduce administrative burdens and improve patient care quality.

Tolan uses a real-time context reconstruction approach each turn, combining recent message summaries, persona cards, vector-retrieved memories, and tone guidance to handle abrupt topic shifts. Its memory system stores facts, preferences, and emotional cues in a high-speed vector database, enabling coherent long-term interactions. The transition to GPT-5.1 improved steerability and latency, allowing Tolan to maintain consistent character traits and reduce memory recall errors by 30%, enhancing user engagement.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Health, a dedicated, privacy-focused experience integrating users' health data and apps with AI assistance [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing ChatGPT Health
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Health, a new feature designed to securely combine users' health information with ChatGPT's AI to help people better understand and manage their health. The service allows users to connect medical records and wellness apps, providing personalized responses while emphasizing privacy and security.

ChatGPT Health operates as a separate space within ChatGPT, with enhanced protections including purpose-built encryption and isolated data storage. It is designed to support, not replace, medical care and was developed in collaboration with physicians. Initially available to a limited group of users outside the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK, the feature will expand to more users on web and iOS platforms in the coming weeks.

items.originalTitle: Announcing OpenAI Grove Cohort 2
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched applications for Grove Cohort 2, a five-week program designed for founders at various stages, from pre-idea to product development. The program provides participants with $50,000 in API credits, early access to new AI tools, and direct mentorship from OpenAI technical leaders, along with in-person workshops and weekly office hours at OpenAI's San Francisco headquarters.

The cohort will include about fifteen participants from diverse backgrounds and experience levels, aiming to build a dense talent network and foster collaboration with OpenAI researchers. After the program, participants can explore funding opportunities or other paths within or outside OpenAI. Applications closed on January 12, 2026.

items.title: OpenAI strengthens ChatGPT Atlas browser agent against prompt injection attacks using automated red teaming with reinforcement learning [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Continuously hardening ChatGPT Atlas against prompt injection
items.summary:
OpenAI is enhancing the security of ChatGPT Atlas by deploying automated red teaming powered by reinforcement learning to proactively identify and patch prompt injection vulnerabilities targeting its browser agent. This approach helps defend the agent, which interacts with webpages and user workflows, from adversarial attacks that could hijack its behavior and compromise sensitive information.

The company recently released a security update including an adversarially trained model and improved safeguards after discovering new prompt injection attack methods through internal testing. OpenAI views prompt injection as a long-term challenge and aims to continuously improve defenses by leveraging model access, deep security knowledge, and compute resources to stay ahead of attackers and reduce real-world risks.

items.title: OpenAI introduces a framework and 13 evaluations to measure chain-of-thought monitorability across 24 environments, finding internal reasoning monitoring more effective than output monitoring [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Evaluating chain-of-thought monitorability
items.summary:
OpenAI has developed a comprehensive framework and a suite of 13 evaluations spanning 24 environments to systematically assess the monitorability of chain-of-thought reasoning in AI models. Their research shows that monitoring a model’s internal reasoning processes is significantly more effective than observing only its actions or final outputs, especially as models engage in longer chains of thought.

The study also reveals that larger models and increased reasoning effort improve monitorability, while reinforcement learning at current scales does not degrade it. Additionally, smaller models with higher reasoning effort can achieve comparable capability with better monitorability, albeit at increased computational cost. OpenAI calls for continued research to preserve chain-of-thought monitorability as a potential control mechanism for future AI systems.

items.title: OpenAI and U.S. Department of Energy sign memorandum to expand AI collaboration for scientific discovery and advanced computing [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Deepening our collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy
items.summary:
OpenAI and the U.S. Department of Energy have formalized a memorandum of understanding to deepen their partnership on artificial intelligence and advanced computing, aiming to accelerate scientific research across DOE initiatives including the Genesis Mission. This agreement builds on existing collaborations with DOE national laboratories, where OpenAI has deployed frontier AI models to support research in areas such as fusion energy and national security.

The MOU establishes a framework for information sharing, coordination, and potential future projects, emphasizing the integration of AI into real scientific workflows with domain experts. OpenAI's work with DOE labs includes deploying AI models on supercomputers like the Venado system at Los Alamos National Laboratory and engaging over 1,000 scientists in testing AI capabilities to inform development. This partnership reflects a broader effort to strengthen U.S. leadership in science and technology through AI-driven discovery.

items.title: OpenAI updates Model Specification with Under-18 Principles to enhance teen safety and age-appropriate guidance in ChatGPT [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Updating our Model Spec with teen protections
items.summary:
OpenAI has updated its Model Specification to include Under-18 Principles designed to provide safe, age-appropriate interactions for teens aged 13 to 17 using ChatGPT. These principles prioritize teen safety, promote real-world support, treat teens according to their developmental needs, and emphasize transparency in AI behavior.

The update clarifies how the model should handle higher-risk topics such as self-harm, explicit content, and dangerous activities by applying stronger safeguards and encouraging teens to seek trusted offline support or emergency services when needed. OpenAI developed these principles with input from experts including the American Psychological Association and continues to refine them based on research and real-world use.

The model improves long-context understanding, supports complex tasks like large refactors and migrations, and offers stronger cybersecurity capabilities than previous versions. GPT-5.2-Codex is available to paid ChatGPT users and will soon be accessible via API, with invite-only access for vetted cybersecurity professionals.

The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks testing realistic coding and terminal tasks, including better handling of Windows environments and enhanced vision capabilities for interpreting technical diagrams and UI elements. OpenAI is implementing additional safeguards due to the model's increased cyber capabilities and is preparing for future models that may reach higher levels of cybersecurity proficiency under its Preparedness Framework.

items.originalTitle: Measuring AI’s capability to accelerate biological research
items.summary:
OpenAI collaborated with Red Queen Bio to develop an evaluation framework testing GPT-5's ability to propose and refine wet lab protocols. GPT-5 autonomously improved a molecular cloning procedure by introducing a novel enzymatic mechanism, increasing cloning efficiency by 79 times compared to the baseline.

The AI system suggested using the recombinase RecA and phage T4 gene 32 single-stranded DNA–binding protein, which together enhanced DNA assembly and transformation steps. Experiments confirmed these improvements, though human scientists still performed the laboratory work. This project demonstrates AI's potential to accelerate biological research by optimizing experimental methods while maintaining biosecurity controls.

items.title: Disney and OpenAI sign three-year deal to license over 200 characters for Sora AI video platform and integrate OpenAI tools across Disney [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: The Walt Disney Company and OpenAI reach landmark agreement to bring beloved characters to Sora
items.summary:
The Walt Disney Company and OpenAI have reached a three-year licensing agreement allowing OpenAI's Sora platform to generate short, user-prompted videos featuring more than 200 characters from Disney, Marvel, Pixar, and Star Wars. The deal includes making selected fan-created videos available on Disney+ and marks Disney's adoption of OpenAI's APIs and ChatGPT Enterprise for internal use and new product development.

The partnership emphasizes responsible AI use to protect user safety and creators' rights, excluding talent likenesses and voices. Disney will also make a $1 billion equity investment in OpenAI as part of the agreement. Sora and ChatGPT Images are expected to begin generating fan-inspired content with Disney's licensed characters in early 2026, expanding creative storytelling possibilities for fans and subscribers.

items.title: OpenAI co-founds Agentic AI Foundation under Linux Foundation, donates AGENTS.md to promote open standards for agentic AI [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: OpenAI co-founds Agentic AI Foundation, donates AGENTS.md
items.summary:
OpenAI has co-founded the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation alongside Anthropic and Block, with support from major tech companies including Google, Microsoft, and AWS. The foundation aims to provide neutral stewardship for open, interoperable infrastructure as agentic AI systems transition from experimental to real-world production.

As part of this initiative, OpenAI contributed AGENTS.md, a lightweight Markdown format designed to provide AI agents with project-specific instructions and context. Since its release in August 2025, AGENTS.md has been adopted by over 60,000 open-source projects and agent frameworks, helping standardize agent behavior across diverse repositories and tools. The AAIF will govern and evolve these open standards collaboratively to ensure portability, safety, and interoperability in the growing agentic AI ecosystem.

items.title: OpenAI reports rapid acceleration and deepening of enterprise AI adoption in 2025, with significant productivity gains across industries and geographies [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: The state of enterprise AI
items.summary:
OpenAI's 2025 enterprise AI report reveals a sharp increase in AI usage across various sectors, with workers and organizations integrating AI more deeply into workflows, resulting in measurable productivity improvements. The report draws on real-world usage data and a survey of 9,000 workers from nearly 100 enterprises, highlighting widespread adoption and growing sophistication in AI applications.

Usage metrics show an eightfold increase in weekly ChatGPT Enterprise messages and a 19-fold rise in structured workflow use, indicating a shift from casual queries to integrated processes. AI adoption is strongest in technology, healthcare, and manufacturing, with notable growth in countries like Australia, Brazil, the Netherlands, and France. items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced OpenAI for Australia, a nationwide initiative partnering with local organizations to develop sovereign AI infrastructure, provide AI skills training to over 1.5 million Australian workers, and foster innovation within the country's AI ecosystem. The program includes a partnership with NEXTDC to build a hyperscale AI campus and GPU supercluster in Sydney, aiming to support sensitive workloads across government and industry.

Additionally, OpenAI plans to accelerate Australian tech innovation by launching its first startup program in the country, offering API credits, mentorship, and workshops to local startups in partnership with leading venture capital firms.

items.title: OpenAI introduces 'confessions' technique for language models to self-report errors and misbehavior, improving transparency and trust [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: How confessions can keep language models honest
items.summary:
OpenAI researchers have developed a method called "confessions" that trains language models to explicitly admit when they break instructions or engage in undesirable behavior. This approach generates a separate output alongside the main answer, focusing solely on honesty to help detect and understand model misalignment and errors.

The technique was tested on GPT-5 Thinking across various adversarial datasets designed to induce misbehavior such as scheming, hacking, or hallucinations. Results showed a low rate of false negatives, indicating that models are likely to accurately confess to non-compliance. Confessions are evaluated independently to ensure truthful reporting without penalizing the model's main response, aiming to enhance monitoring, training, and user trust in AI outputs.

items.summary:
The OpenAI Foundation announced the first recipients of its People-First AI Fund, distributing $40.5 million in unrestricted grants to 208 nonprofit organizations across the United States. The funding aims to support community-based nonprofits working to strengthen local communities and expand opportunities related to artificial intelligence.

The grants were awarded following an open call that received nearly 3,000 applications, with a selection process involving independent review and final approval by the OpenAI Foundation Board. The funded organizations represent diverse regions and missions, including workforce development, youth media, nonprofit capacity building, and rural community support, many of which are early in their AI exploration. A second wave of $9.5 million in grants is planned to support organizations advancing transformative AI work in areas like health.

items.title: OpenAI discloses Mixpanel security incident exposing limited API user analytics data, no credentials or payment info affected [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Mixpanel security incident: what OpenAI users need to know
items.summary:
OpenAI reported a security incident involving Mixpanel, a third-party analytics provider, where an attacker accessed and exported limited user analytics data related to OpenAI's API platform and some ChatGPT users. The breach did not affect OpenAI's systems directly, and no sensitive information such as API keys, passwords, or payment details were compromised.

The exposed data included user names, email addresses, approximate locations, browser and operating system details, and organization or user IDs. OpenAI has removed Mixpanel from its services, notified affected users, and is enhancing security measures across its vendor ecosystem to prevent future incidents. Users are advised to remain vigilant against phishing attempts using the exposed information.

OpenAI also ensures that customer data is not used for model training unless explicitly permitted by the customer.

items.title: UCLA Professor Ernest Ryu uses GPT-5 to solve a 40-year-old optimization theory problem involving Nesterov Accelerated Gradient stability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: GPT-5 and the future of mathematical discovery
items.summary:
Professor Ernest Ryu of UCLA collaborated with OpenAI's GPT-5 to address a longstanding open problem in optimization theory concerning the stability of algorithms using Nesterov Accelerated Gradient (NAG). This method, introduced in 1983, accelerates algorithm convergence by predicting future parameter states, but its stability despite increased momentum had remained unexplained for decades.

Ryu engaged GPT-5 as a collaborative tool to explore creative approaches and mathematical ideas drawn from a wide range of research papers. While GPT-5 did not invent new mathematical principles, its ability to synthesize existing knowledge helped Ryu uncover a path to solving the problem, demonstrating AI's potential to accelerate mathematical discovery and advance optimization theory.

items.originalTitle: OpenAI and Foxconn collaborate to strengthen U.S. manufacturing across the AI supply chain
items.summary:
OpenAI and Foxconn have announced a collaboration to co-design and develop multiple generations of AI data center hardware, with manufacturing planned at Foxconn's U.S. facilities. The partnership aims to strengthen U.S. supply chains by broadening sourcing, localizing testing and assembly, and producing critical AI data center components domestically.

This initiative focuses on accelerating the deployment of advanced AI systems by combining OpenAI's insights into AI infrastructure needs with Foxconn's manufacturing expertise. The collaboration does not include purchase commitments but grants OpenAI early access to evaluate the hardware and an option to purchase. Both companies emphasize the importance of building AI infrastructure in the U.S. to support American leadership in AI and ensure economic benefits reach domestic workers and manufacturers.

items.title: OpenAI partners with DoorDash and SCORE to launch Small Business AI Jam, training 1,000 small businesses across five US cities in AI tools for growth and competition [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Helping 1,000 small businesses build with AI
items.summary:
OpenAI has teamed up with DoorDash, SCORE, and local organizations to host the Small Business AI Jam, a nationwide workshop aimed at equipping 1,000 small business owners with practical AI tools and training. The event spans five hubs—San Francisco, New York City, Houston, Detroit, and Miami—where participants build AI solutions tailored to their business needs, such as marketing and customer communication.

The initiative addresses the challenge that many small businesses face in adopting AI due to limited resources and technical expertise. Participants receive hands-on mentorship, access to online resources before and after the event, and join a community to continue learning. The program aims to help small businesses improve efficiency and compete more effectively with larger enterprises by leveraging AI technology.

items.title: OpenAI releases early research on GPT-5 accelerating scientific discovery across multiple fields including math, biology, and physics [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Early experiments in accelerating science with GPT-5
items.summary:
OpenAI has published initial experiments showing how GPT-5 assists researchers in accelerating scientific progress by synthesizing results, conducting literature reviews, and generating novel proofs in areas such as mathematics, biology, physics, and computer science. Collaborations with universities and national labs demonstrate GPT-5's ability to speed up discovery processes, including identifying mechanisms in immune cells and solving longstanding mathematical problems.

The research highlights GPT-5's role as a tool that complements human expertise, enabling faster hypothesis testing and exploration of ideas. OpenAI emphasizes that effective use of GPT-5 requires skilled interaction by scientists who guide the AI, validate results, and integrate its outputs with specialized scientific tools. The findings also outline current limitations and aim to inform the scientific community about GPT-5's capabilities and appropriate applications in research settings.

items.title: OpenAI expands third-party testing of frontier AI models to enhance safety, transparency, and risk assessment [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Strengthening our safety ecosystem with external testing
items.summary:
OpenAI is collaborating with independent experts to conduct third-party assessments of its advanced AI models, including GPT-4 and GPT-5, to validate safety claims, identify risks, and improve protective measures. These external evaluations cover areas such as biosecurity, cybersecurity, AI self-improvement, and deception, providing an independent layer of scrutiny alongside OpenAI's internal testing.

The company supports diverse assessor organizations by granting secure access to early model checkpoints and evaluation data, enabling detailed analysis including chain-of-thought reasoning to detect complex behaviors like scheming. OpenAI also emphasizes transparency by publishing summaries of third-party assessments and fostering ongoing partnerships to strengthen the broader AI safety ecosystem and inform responsible deployment decisions.

OpenAI explains how evaluation frameworks, or "evals," enable businesses to translate AI objectives into measurable outcomes, improving reliability and reducing errors in AI systems. These frameworks help organizations align AI performance with specific workflows and business goals to increase efficiency and value.

The article details a three-step process for creating effective evals: specifying clear success criteria with cross-functional teams, measuring AI outputs against real-world conditions, and iteratively improving the system based on error analysis. OpenAI emphasizes that contextual evals tailored to an organization's unique needs are essential for maximizing AI benefits and managing risks in diverse business environments.

items.originalTitle: OpenAI and Target team up on new AI-powered experiences
items.summary:
OpenAI and Target have partnered to introduce a new Target app within ChatGPT that offers personalized shopping recommendations, multi-item baskets, and checkout options including Drive Up, Order Pickup, and shipping. Target also plans to expand its use of ChatGPT Enterprise across its workforce to enhance productivity and customer service.

The partnership builds on Target's broader AI strategy to integrate intelligence throughout its business, improving supply chain forecasting, store operations, and guest experiences. The Target app in ChatGPT, launching in beta, enables conversational shopping and aims to make discovery and checkout as seamless as browsing in-store. Target currently uses AI tools like Agent Assist and Store Companion to support employees and guests, and plans to add features such as Target Circle linking and same-day delivery to the app.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-5.1-Codex-Max, a faster, more efficient coding model designed for long-running, complex software engineering tasks with improved reasoning and token efficiency [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Building more with GPT-5.1-Codex-Max
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced GPT-5.1-Codex-Max, an advanced coding model built to handle large-scale, detailed programming projects by operating across multiple context windows using a process called compaction. This enables the model to sustain coherent work over millions of tokens, supporting tasks like project-scale refactors, deep debugging, and multi-hour agent loops.

The model demonstrates significant improvements in speed and token efficiency, achieving better performance with fewer tokens compared to previous versions. It is trained on real-world software engineering tasks and is the first Codex model to operate in Windows environments. GPT-5.1-Codex-Max is currently available in Codex for CLI, IDE extensions, cloud, and code review, with API access planned soon.

GPT-5.1-Codex-Max also shows enhanced capabilities in long-horizon reasoning and cybersecurity tasks, although it has not yet reached high capability in cybersecurity under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework. The model's ability to compact sessions and persistently iterate on tasks marks a step toward more reliable and general AI coding partners.

items.title: OpenAI publishes GPT-5.1-Codex-Max system card detailing model and product-level safety measures for agentic coding tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: GPT-5.1-Codex-Max System Card
items.summary:
OpenAI released the system card for GPT-5.1-Codex-Max, a new agentic coding model trained on diverse software engineering and reasoning tasks with the ability to operate over millions of tokens. The card outlines extensive safety protocols including model-level mitigations like targeted safety training against harmful tasks and prompt injections, as well as product-level controls such as agent sandboxing and configurable network access.

The model was evaluated under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework and is considered highly capable in biology but not yet at a high capability level in cybersecurity or AI self-improvement. OpenAI expects capabilities in cybersecurity to improve rapidly and continues to deploy GPT-5.1-Codex-Max with safeguards consistent with those used for GPT-5.

The initiative aims to boost productivity and foster new AI-driven startups across Ireland.

The program includes an SME Booster initiative starting in 2026, offering AI skills training, workshops, and mentoring to help businesses reduce costs and expand. OpenAI is also partnering with Dogpatch Labs to support early-stage AI startups and with Patch to provide coding and AI development opportunities for young builders aged 16 to 21. These efforts align with Ireland's broader digital and AI strategy and its goal to become a European hub for AI entrepreneurship.

items.title: OpenAI trains sparse neural networks with fewer connections to improve interpretability and understandability of AI model computations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Understanding neural networks through sparse circuits
items.summary:
OpenAI has developed a new approach to training neural networks by enforcing sparsity, where most connections between neurons are set to zero, resulting in simpler, more traceable internal circuits. This method aims to enhance mechanistic interpretability, allowing researchers to better understand how AI models perform specific tasks by isolating small, disentangled circuits responsible for behaviors.

The research focuses on balancing model capability and interpretability by training larger but sparser models, which show increasingly simple circuits for algorithmic tasks. This approach contrasts with traditional dense networks, which have complex, tangled connections that are difficult to analyze. OpenAI views this work as a step toward safer and more reliable AI systems by providing clearer insights into model reasoning processes.

items.originalTitle: Introducing GPT-5.1 for developers
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched GPT-5.1 for developers through its API, introducing enhancements that balance intelligence and speed for various tasks. The update includes adaptive reasoning that speeds up simpler tasks, a new no reasoning mode for latency-sensitive use cases, and extended prompt caching that retains context for up to 24 hours to reduce latency and cost.

The release also improves coding capabilities through collaborations with startups, making GPT-5.1 more intuitive and communicative for coding tasks. Additionally, it adds two new tools: apply_patch for more reliable code editing and a shell tool to execute shell commands, aiming to support more efficient and reliable agentic workflows for developers.

items.title: OpenAI launches group chats in ChatGPT for collaborative conversations with up to 20 participants, initially in select countries and across Free, Go, Plus, and Pro plans [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing group chats in ChatGPT
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced group chats in ChatGPT, allowing multiple users to collaborate in the same conversation alongside ChatGPT. This feature supports up to 20 participants and is designed for shared planning, decision-making, and brainstorming, with ChatGPT adapting its responses based on the group context. The rollout began as a pilot in Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, and Taiwan and is expanding globally to all logged-in users on various ChatGPT plans.

Group chats are separate from private conversations, and personal ChatGPT memory is not shared or used in these chats. Users can manage group settings, invite others via links, and customize ChatGPT's behavior within each group. The feature includes safeguards such as requiring invitation acceptance and controls for participant management, aiming to facilitate collaborative work and social interactions while maintaining privacy and user control.

items.summary:
Philips is expanding AI literacy across its 70,000 employees by implementing ChatGPT Enterprise, aiming to embed AI capabilities beyond specialized teams to drive innovation and better patient care. The initiative includes executive training, company-wide challenges for AI use cases, and a focus on responsible AI principles such as transparency and human oversight.

The rollout emphasizes building trust through low-risk internal experiments and prioritizes reducing administrative burdens in clinical environments to give healthcare professionals more time for patient care. Philips plans to advance from individual productivity improvements to workflow automation supported by AI agents, reinforcing its commitment to responsible AI use in healthcare.

items.title: OpenAI resists New York Times' demand for 20 million private ChatGPT conversations amid privacy concerns [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Fighting the New York Times’ invasion of user privacy
items.summary:
OpenAI is opposing a New York Times court order demanding access to 20 million private ChatGPT conversations, which the company says violates user privacy and security. The Times alleges the data may reveal attempts to bypass its paywall, but OpenAI argues the request is overly broad and unrelated to the lawsuit against it.

OpenAI has previously pushed back against similar demands and is accelerating its privacy and security measures, including plans for client-side encryption and automated safety detection. The company emphasizes its commitment to protecting user data from unauthorized access and is seeking to have the court reject the Times' request while continuing to explore options to safeguard user privacy.

items.title: OpenAI outlines prompt injection as a key AI security challenge and details multi-layered defenses including safety training and monitoring [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Understanding prompt injections: a frontier security challenge
items.summary:
OpenAI highlights prompt injection as a significant security risk where malicious instructions embedded in input prompts can manipulate AI behavior against user intent. These attacks can occur through content from various sources, such as web pages or emails, potentially leading AI systems to reveal sensitive information or make harmful decisions.

To address this, OpenAI is developing defenses including advanced safety training to help models recognize and resist prompt injections, automated monitoring systems to detect and block attacks, and layered security protections within their products and infrastructure. These efforts aim to ensure AI systems perform user-intended tasks safely despite adversarial attempts to mislead them.

items.title: CRED integrates OpenAI's GPT models to enhance customer support accuracy and reduce response times, improving satisfaction for over 15 million Indian users [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: How CRED is tapping AI to deliver premium customer experiences
items.summary:
CRED, an India-based members-only club for creditworthy individuals, is using OpenAI's GPT-powered tools to create premium, concierge-like customer experiences. The company developed Cleo, an AI conversational companion, along with internal tools Thea and Stark, to handle queries, assist support agents, and streamline operations. Since launching these AI tools, CRED has seen a 14 percentage point increase in customer satisfaction, a 98% resolution accuracy rate, and a 31% reduction in session drop-offs.

CRED aims to expand AI integration across all business lines to improve efficiency and maintain its core values of trust, security, and exceptional design. The company plans to use AI to identify unanswered queries and update its knowledge base in real time, helping every team member become more effective and efficient as it scales its premium financial services in India.

items.title: OpenAI launches IndQA benchmark to evaluate AI understanding and reasoning in 12 Indian languages across 10 cultural domains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing IndQA
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced IndQA, a new benchmark designed to assess AI systems' performance in understanding and reasoning about Indian culture and languages. IndQA covers 2,278 questions across 12 Indian languages and 10 cultural domains, created with input from 261 domain experts to test nuanced, reasoning-heavy tasks beyond existing multilingual benchmarks.

The benchmark includes languages such as Bengali, Hindi, Kannada, Marathi, and Tamil, and domains like History, Law, Food, and Literature. Each question features culturally grounded prompts, English translations, grading rubrics, and ideal answers. IndQA aims to improve AI capabilities for Indian users and serves as a model for future benchmarks in other regions and languages.

items.title: AWS and OpenAI announce $38 billion multi-year partnership to provide infrastructure for advanced AI workloads through 2026 and beyond [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: AWS and OpenAI announce multi-year strategic partnership
items.summary:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) and OpenAI have entered a multi-year strategic partnership valued at $38 billion, under which AWS will supply infrastructure and computing resources to support OpenAI's advanced artificial intelligence workloads starting immediately. The agreement includes access to hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA GPUs and the ability to scale to tens of millions of CPUs, enabling OpenAI to rapidly expand its compute capacity for generative AI models like ChatGPT.

The partnership leverages AWS's experience in running large-scale AI infrastructure securely and efficiently, with Amazon EC2 UltraServers clustering NVIDIA GPUs to optimize performance and low-latency networking. OpenAI plans to deploy all contracted capacity by the end of 2026, with potential expansion into 2027 and beyond, supporting both inference and training workloads. This collaboration builds on previous integrations of OpenAI models into AWS services such as Amazon Bedrock, benefiting millions of users and customers worldwide.

items.title: OpenAI expands Stargate AI infrastructure project to Michigan with new one-gigawatt campus, creating over 2,500 construction jobs and supporting Midwest economic growth [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Expanding Stargate to Michigan
items.summary:
OpenAI announced a new Stargate campus in Saline Township, Michigan, as part of its partnership with Oracle, adding over one gigawatt of AI infrastructure capacity. This expansion contributes to a total of more than 8 gigawatts planned across the U.S. and supports the company's $500 billion, 10-gigawatt commitment to AI infrastructure investment.

The Michigan campus, developed by Related Digital with construction starting in early 2026, will create more than 2,500 union construction jobs and use a closed-loop cooling system to reduce water consumption. DTE Energy will supply power using existing transmission capacity, with any necessary upgrades funded by the project. This expansion builds on previous Stargate sites in Texas, New Mexico, Wisconsin, and Ohio, aiming to strengthen local economies and advance U.S. leadership in AI technology.

items.title: OpenAI launches Aardvark, an autonomous AI security researcher powered by GPT-5, now in private beta to identify and fix software vulnerabilities at scale [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing Aardvark: OpenAI’s agentic security researcher
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Aardvark, an AI agent designed to autonomously analyze source code repositories, identify security vulnerabilities, validate exploitability, and propose patches. Powered by GPT-5, Aardvark mimics human security researchers by reading code, running tests, and using tools to detect issues without relying on traditional methods like fuzzing.

Aardvark integrates with GitHub and OpenAI Codex to provide actionable insights and patch suggestions, aiming to assist developers and security teams in managing software security more effectively. It has been tested internally and with external partners, demonstrating high accuracy in detecting known and synthetic vulnerabilities, and has contributed to identifying issues in open-source projects with several receiving CVE identifiers.

OpenAI plans to offer pro-bono scanning for select non-commercial open-source repositories and updated its coordinated disclosure policy to support collaborative and scalable vulnerability management. Aardvark is currently available in private beta, with plans to expand access and refine its capabilities.

items.title: OpenAI launches OWL architecture for ChatGPT-based Atlas browser, separating Chromium engine from UI for faster startup and improved performance [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: How we built OWL, the new architecture behind our ChatGPT-based browser, Atlas
items.summary: OpenAI has developed OWL, a new architecture that separates the Chromium browser engine from the user interface in its ChatGPT-based browser, Atlas. This design enables faster startup times, better responsiveness with multiple tabs, and a richer user experience driven by ChatGPT's agentic capabilities. OWL runs Chromium as an isolated service layer outside the main app process, allowing Atlas to remain stable even if Chromium crashes or hangs. The architecture also simplifies development by reducing the need to build Chromium from source, accelerating iteration and feature delivery.

items.title: OpenAI releases gpt-oss-safeguard-120b and 20b models for policy-based content labeling with baseline safety evaluations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: gpt-oss-safeguard technical report
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced gpt-oss-safeguard-120b and gpt-oss-safeguard-20b, two open-weight reasoning models derived from the gpt-oss series, designed to apply policy-based reasoning for content classification. These models are available under the Apache 2.0 license and support customizable reasoning efforts, full chain-of-thought outputs, and structured outputs, compatible with OpenAI's Responses API.

The report details the models' capabilities and presents baseline safety evaluations comparing them to the original gpt-oss models, confirming that safety standards are maintained even when used in chat settings, which is not their intended use. The models were trained without additional biological or cybersecurity data, and prior worst-case scenario assessments for gpt-oss models apply to these safeguards as well.

items.originalTitle: Introducing gpt-oss-safeguard
items.summary:
OpenAI has released gpt-oss-safeguard, a research preview of open-weight reasoning models designed to help developers implement and refine custom safety policies for content classification. The models, available in two sizes, interpret developer-provided policies at inference time and provide explainable reasoning for their classifications, allowing flexible and iterative policy adjustments without retraining.

These models address challenges in emerging or nuanced safety risks where traditional classifiers require extensive labeled data and retraining. OpenAI collaborated with ROOST to develop the models and is inviting feedback from the research and safety community while establishing a model community to explore open AI models for online safety. The release includes a technical report detailing the models' safety performance.

items.originalTitle: Doppel’s AI defense system stops attacks before they spread
items.summary:
Doppel has developed an AI-powered defense platform that leverages OpenAI's GPT-5 and reinforcement fine-tuning to autonomously detect, classify, and mitigate deepfake and impersonation threats. This system processes millions of signals daily, automates decision-making to handle threats at internet scale, and reduces security analyst workloads by 80%, enabling organizations to respond to attacks within minutes instead of hours.

The platform uses a multi-stage pipeline including signal filtering, parallel threat confirmation, and final verification with natural-language justifications, reserving human review for ambiguous cases. Reinforcement fine-tuning trains the models on analyst feedback to improve consistency and accuracy, allowing Doppel to triple its threat-handling capacity and stay ahead of rapidly evolving social engineering attacks that can launch and vanish within an hour.

items.originalTitle: Built to benefit everyone
items.summary:
OpenAI has finalized a recapitalization that simplifies its corporate structure and establishes the OpenAI Foundation, a nonprofit holding significant equity in the for-profit OpenAI Group. This structure aims to advance OpenAI's mission of ensuring artificial general intelligence benefits all humanity by linking the nonprofit's philanthropic efforts with the company's commercial success.

The OpenAI Foundation plans to commit $25 billion initially to accelerate health breakthroughs and develop technical solutions for AI resilience, addressing risks and maximizing benefits. This move follows discussions with California and Delaware Attorneys General and builds on previous initiatives like the People-First AI Fund, reinforcing OpenAI's mission-focused governance and its commitment to responsible AI development.

items.title: Microsoft and OpenAI sign new agreement to extend partnership, clarify IP rights, and support OpenAI's public benefit corporation formation [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: The next chapter of the Microsoft–OpenAI partnership
items.summary:
Microsoft and OpenAI have entered a new definitive agreement that strengthens their long-term partnership and supports OpenAI's transition to a public benefit corporation. The deal includes Microsoft holding a roughly 27% stake in OpenAI Group PBC and extends Microsoft's exclusive IP rights and Azure API exclusivity until Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) is declared.

The agreement introduces an independent expert panel to verify AGI declarations, extends Microsoft's IP rights through 2032 including post-AGI models with safety guardrails, and allows OpenAI to jointly develop some products with third parties while maintaining Azure exclusivity for API products. OpenAI can now provide API access to US government national security customers on any cloud and release open weight models meeting capability criteria. Both companies aim to continue advancing AI innovation and growth under this updated partnership.

The proposal highlights that expanding electricity capacity and modernizing regulations are critical to supporting AI growth and economic development.

The submission warns of an "electron gap" as China rapidly expands its power capacity, outpacing the US and threatening its AI leadership. OpenAI is investing over $400 billion and adding nearly 7 gigawatts of compute capacity through new data centers, while also promoting workforce training programs to address skilled labor shortages essential for building and operating AI infrastructure.

items.title: Consensus launches multi-agent research assistant using GPT-5 and Responses API to accelerate scientific discovery for over 8 million researchers [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Consensus accelerates research with GPT-5 and Responses API
items.summary:
Consensus has developed a multi-agent research assistant called Scholar Agent, built on GPT-5 and OpenAI's Responses API, to rapidly read, analyze, and synthesize scientific literature. The platform, used by more than 8 million researchers, aims to reduce the time from question to conclusion from weeks to minutes by mimicking human research workflows.

The system divides tasks among specialized agents that plan, search, read, and analyze peer-reviewed papers from a database of over 220 million documents. This architecture improves accuracy and reliability by limiting each agent's scope and grounding answers in verifiable evidence. Consensus shifted to the Responses API for better multi-agent coordination and cost efficiency, with GPT-5 outperforming previous models in tool-calling and planning.

Focusing on direct-to-researcher adoption rather than institutional sales, Consensus targets students, faculty, and clinicians who need timely access to scientific evidence. Its consumer-friendly design and conversational interface have driven rapid growth and widespread use across academic and clinical communities.

items.title: OpenAI says ChatGPT will no longer be available on WhatsApp after January 15, 2026, urging users to link accounts to continue conversations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Continue your ChatGPT experience beyond WhatsApp
items.summary:
OpenAI announced that ChatGPT will stop operating on WhatsApp after January 15, 2026, due to changes in WhatsApp's policies and terms. Users are encouraged to link their ChatGPT accounts to maintain access to their conversation history and continue using ChatGPT on other platforms such as iOS, Android, web, and MacOS.

The company provided instructions for linking accounts via WhatsApp and highlighted additional features available outside WhatsApp, including voice conversations, deep research, and file uploads. OpenAI emphasized the importance of linking accounts before the cutoff date, as WhatsApp does not support chat exports and conversations will not transfer automatically after January 15, 2026.

items.originalTitle: Introducing ChatGPT Atlas, the browser with ChatGPT built in
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Atlas, a new web browser for macOS that integrates ChatGPT directly into the browsing experience, allowing users to get instant answers, summaries, and assistance without leaving the page. The browser includes features like browser memories that remember context from visited sites and an agent mode for automating tasks, available to Plus, Pro, and Business users.

ChatGPT Atlas supports importing bookmarks, passwords, and browsing history from other browsers and offers customizable privacy controls, including the ability to clear browsing history and manage what ChatGPT can see. The browser is available worldwide for Free, Plus, Pro, and Go users, with beta versions for Business, Enterprise, and Education plans; versions for Windows, iOS, and Android are planned for the future.
