items.originalTitle: Plex Coffee delivers fast, personal service with ChatGPT
items.summary:
Plex Coffee implemented ChatGPT Business to address challenges in training and knowledge sharing as it expanded from one to four cafés. The tool centralizes information from Notion and delivers it in natural language, reducing WhatsApp operational queries by more than half and shortening onboarding from weeks to days.

The company also uses ChatGPT Business for expansion research, demand analysis, and automating supply orders, allowing store managers to focus more on community engagement and improving operational efficiency across locations.

items.originalTitle: Expert Council on Well-Being and AI
items.summary:
OpenAI has established an Expert Council on Well-Being and AI composed of psychologists, clinicians, and researchers to advise on creating safer and more empathetic AI interactions, particularly for teenagers. The council aims to define healthy AI interactions and support emotional health through ChatGPT and related products.

The council includes experts in psychology, psychiatry, human-computer interaction, and youth development, who have already contributed to features like parental controls and distress notifications for teens. OpenAI plans ongoing collaboration with the council and other health professionals to ensure AI systems promote well-being and respond appropriately in sensitive situations.

This initiative complements OpenAI's broader safety efforts, including work with the Global Physician Network to ground AI behavior in clinical best practices. The company intends to continue refining ChatGPT based on expert guidance to enhance its positive impact on users' mental health and well-being.

items.title: HYGH integrates ChatGPT Business to accelerate software development and campaign delivery, cutting turnaround times and boosting output scalability [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: HYGH speeds development and campaigns with ChatGPT Business
items.summary:
HYGH, a German digital media company managing over 4,000 digital displays, has integrated ChatGPT Business into its operations to speed up software development and campaign creation. This adoption has enabled the company to reduce turnaround times, increase the number of weekly minimum viable products from one every 1-2 months to two per week, and enhance creative output for advertisers.

The company uses ChatGPT Business for tasks ranging from product requirement documentation and coding to generating campaign mock-ups and internal collaboration. Employees save an estimated 5.5 hours per week each, and the platform supports GDPR-compliant data handling. HYGH also hosts regular sessions to share AI best practices, embedding AI into its operating model to improve efficiency and creativity.

HYGH's co-founder Antonius Link emphasizes that AI is essential for staying competitive, noting that the company has already launched campaign preview tools using OpenAI APIs that allow advertisers to visualize products on digital screens instantly. The integration of ChatGPT Business has contributed to revenue growth and a significant boost in operational speed and scalability.

items.title: OpenAI defines and measures political bias in ChatGPT using real-world prompts, finds less than 0.01% biased responses, and reports GPT-5 reduces bias by 30% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Defining and evaluating political bias in LLMs
items.summary: OpenAI has developed a new evaluation framework to define and measure political bias in ChatGPT, using around 500 prompts across 100 topics that reflect real-world usage. Their analysis shows the models remain near-objective on neutral prompts but exhibit moderate bias on emotionally charged ones, with less than 0.01% of production responses showing political bias. GPT-5 models demonstrate a 30% reduction in bias compared to earlier versions. The evaluation focuses on text-based interactions in U.S. English and aims to improve model objectivity, especially in challenging contexts where bias is more likely to emerge.

Since February 2024, the company has banned violating accounts and shared insights with partners to improve user protections and raise awareness of AI misuse.

OpenAI continues to enforce policies, publish public threat reports, and collaborate with peers to safeguard users and promote responsible AI deployment.

items.summary:

Since its research preview launch in May, Codex has seen significant adoption, with daily usage growing over tenfold since August and integration at companies like Cisco and Instacart. The new Slack integration allows users to interact with Codex directly in team channels, while the SDK supports embedding Codex capabilities into custom applications. Admins gain more control through environment management and analytics dashboards to oversee Codex usage and code review quality.

OpenAI highlights that Codex has become integral to engineering workflows internally and externally, helping reduce code review times and automate code cleanup, thereby accelerating development velocity and improving code quality across various organizations.

items.originalTitle: Introducing apps in ChatGPT and the new Apps SDK
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced a new generation of interactive apps integrated directly within ChatGPT, allowing users to engage with services like Spotify, Zillow, and Canva through natural language conversation. The apps are available in preview to ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, and Edu customers, as well as users on Free, Go, Plus, and Pro plans outside the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK.

Developers can start building and testing apps using the newly released Apps SDK, which is based on the open Model Context Protocol and supports both app logic and interface design. OpenAI plans to accept app submissions for review and publication later this year and aims to expand app availability to EU users soon.

items.originalTitle: AMD and OpenAI announce strategic partnership to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs
items.summary:
AMD and OpenAI have entered a multi-year strategic partnership to deploy a total of 6 gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPUs to power OpenAI's next-generation AI infrastructure, beginning with an initial 1 gigawatt deployment in the second half of 2026. The collaboration builds on previous joint work with AMD's MI300X and MI350X series and aims to advance large-scale AI deployments and innovation.

As part of the agreement, AMD has issued OpenAI warrants for up to 160 million shares of AMD common stock, vesting as deployment milestones and share-price targets are met. Both companies expect the partnership to accelerate AI infrastructure development and generate significant revenue and shareholder value, reinforcing their leadership in high-performance computing and generative AI research.

items.title: OpenAI and Allied for Startups release Hacktivate AI report with 20 policy proposals to boost AI adoption and competitiveness in Europe [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Accelerating AI adoption in Europe
items.summary:
OpenAI and Allied for Startups have published the Hacktivate AI report, which presents 20 actionable policy recommendations aimed at accelerating artificial intelligence adoption across Europe and enhancing the continent's competitiveness in the AI sector. The report was developed through a policy hackathon involving 65 participants from EU institutions, governments, enterprises, startups, and AI experts.

The proposals include initiatives such as an Individual AI Learning Account to support professional development, an AI Champions Network to encourage adoption among SMEs, and a European GovAI Hub to share public sector resources. The report emphasizes simplifying regulations and harmonizing policies to strengthen the Digital Single Market. This effort aligns with the upcoming European Commission Apply AI Strategy and builds on OpenAI's broader engagement with European AI policy and education initiatives.

items.title: OpenAI launches AgentKit with tools for building, deploying, and optimizing AI agents, including Agent Builder, Connector Registry, and ChatKit [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing AgentKit, new Evals, and RFT for agents
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced AgentKit, a comprehensive suite of tools designed to help developers and enterprises build, deploy, and optimize AI agents more efficiently. The toolkit includes Agent Builder for visual workflow design, Connector Registry for managing data connections, and ChatKit for embedding customizable chat-based agent experiences.

AgentKit aims to simplify the complex process of creating multi-agent workflows by providing drag-and-drop interfaces, versioning, and safety features like Guardrails. Early adopters such as Ramp and LY Corporation have reported significant reductions in development time, while enterprises can centrally govern data sources across platforms. OpenAI is also expanding evaluation capabilities to improve agent performance and plans to wind down some earlier products by late 2026, recommending AgentKit and Workspace Agents for ongoing workflows.

items.originalTitle: With GPT-5, Wrtn builds lifestyle AI for millions in Korea
items.summary:
Wrtn has developed a Lifestyle AI application using GPT-5 technology that integrates productivity, creativity, and learning features, reaching 6.5 million monthly active users in Korea. The app includes persona-based prompts and localized interactions to provide natural conversations in Korean slang and cadence, appealing to a broad audience from students to professionals and families.

The company employs a modular router architecture to optimize AI model usage, enabling seamless upgrades and improved performance with each OpenAI release. Since adopting GPT-5, Wrtn has seen an 8% increase in daily active users and enhanced capabilities such as better instruction adherence and personalization. Wrtn plans to expand its AI tools across East Asia, leveraging its localization expertise and scalable design.

items.originalTitle: OpenAI announces strategic collaboration with Japan’s Digital Agency
items.summary:
OpenAI and Japan’s Digital Agency announced a strategic collaboration to explore the safe and effective use of generative AI in enhancing Japan’s public services. The partnership includes deploying Gennai, an AI tool powered by OpenAI technology, for government employees and aligns with Japan’s policies on secure government AI.

The collaboration supports the Hiroshima AI Process, an international policy framework led by Japan to promote safe, secure, and trustworthy AI adoption across governments, private sectors, and civil society in Asia and emerging economies. OpenAI plans to pursue ISMAP certification and deepen cooperation with Japanese institutions to ensure responsible integration of generative AI into society.

items.originalTitle: Launching Sora responsibly
items.summary:
OpenAI introduced Sora 2 and the Sora app, combining advanced video generation with collaborative creation while embedding safety measures from the start. These include visible watermarks and metadata for AI content provenance, consent-based controls over user likenesses, and safeguards against harmful content.

The platform restricts mature content for teens, offers parental controls, and prevents unauthorized use of characters or likenesses. It also employs layered defenses to filter unsafe material, monitors audio generation for policy violations, and provides users with control over sharing and reporting content. OpenAI maintains ongoing efforts to address risks associated with realistic video and audio generation in Sora.

items.originalTitle: Sora 2 is here
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched Sora 2, its latest video and audio generation model that offers enhanced physical accuracy, realism, and controllability compared to earlier versions. The model supports synchronized dialogue and sound effects and can simulate complex physical interactions more accurately, such as realistic sports moves and object dynamics. Users can create and remix content using the new Sora app, which also allows them to insert themselves or others into generated scenes through a feature called "characters." 

Sora 2 represents a significant advancement in video generation technology, aiming to better simulate real-world physics and failures rather than producing unrealistic results. The app was initially tested internally at OpenAI and includes tools to help users control their feed and avoid negative social effects. Despite its improvements, the model still makes mistakes but demonstrates progress toward more general-purpose AI simulation capabilities.

items.originalTitle: Combating online child sexual exploitation & abuse
items.summary:
OpenAI is intensifying efforts to prevent the use of its AI models for online child sexual exploitation and abuse by enforcing strict usage policies, removing harmful content from training data, and collaborating with industry partners and authorities. The company prohibits any use of its services for creating or distributing child sexual abuse material (CSAM) or exploitation content and actively monitors and bans violators, reporting incidents to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC).

OpenAI employs advanced detection technologies, including hash matching and content classifiers, to identify and block attempts to generate or upload CSAM. The company also shares insights on emerging abuse patterns with other organizations to improve industry-wide safeguards. These measures are part of OpenAI's broader commitment to developing safe AI and disrupting harmful activities involving minors.

items.title: OpenAI launches parental controls and safety notifications for linked teen ChatGPT accounts, enabling parents to customize settings and monitor usage [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing parental controls
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced parental controls for ChatGPT, allowing parents to link their accounts with their teens' and customize settings to ensure a safe, age-appropriate experience. The new tools include content safeguards, quiet hours, voice mode disablement, memory controls, and image generation restrictions, along with a resource page to support families.

The system also features notifications to alert parents if a linked teen's account shows signs of acute distress or is banned for violent activity, with protections designed to avoid false alarms from non-harmful content. OpenAI developed these controls in consultation with experts and advocacy groups, emphasizing that parental controls complement ongoing conversations about responsible AI use and family involvement.

items.title: OpenAI launches Instant Checkout and open-source Agentic Commerce Protocol in ChatGPT to enable direct purchases from US Etsy sellers and upcoming Shopify merchants [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Buy it in ChatGPT: Instant Checkout and the Agentic Commerce Protocol
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Instant Checkout within ChatGPT, allowing US users to buy products directly from Etsy sellers and soon from over a million Shopify merchants. This feature is powered by the newly open-sourced Agentic Commerce Protocol, developed with Stripe, which facilitates secure, seamless transactions between users, AI agents, and merchants without leaving the chat interface.

The Agentic Commerce Protocol is designed as an open standard to enable AI agents and businesses to collaborate on purchases while keeping merchants in control of payments, fulfillment, and customer relationships. Instant Checkout currently supports single-item purchases with plans to add multi-item carts and expand merchant and regional availability. Merchants can integrate the protocol with minimal changes to their existing systems, and users confirm each transaction step to maintain control and security.

items.originalTitle: Partnering with AARP to help keep older adults safe online
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched a multi-year partnership with AARP and its Older Adults Technology Services (OATS) to help older adults use AI safely and confidently, starting with educational content on spotting scams using ChatGPT. This effort builds on a $2 million commitment to support OATS's Senior Planet program and includes updated AI literacy curricula, digital safety courses, and community-driven training across the U.S.

The collaboration features a new OpenAI Academy video demonstrating how older adults can use ChatGPT as a tool to identify potential scams by recognizing warning signs like urgent language or suspicious links. The initiative also includes annual surveys on AI use among older adults and specialized training for AARP state offices, aiming to make AI education accessible and promote digital safety for this demographic.

items.originalTitle: More ways to work with your team and tools in ChatGPT
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced shared projects, smarter connectors, and new compliance and security features to ChatGPT Business plans, aiming to help teams collaborate more effectively and maintain consistent work. Shared projects allow team members to jointly add files and instructions, enabling ChatGPT to provide tailored responses based on shared context. The update also includes connectors to popular tools like Gmail, Google Calendar, Microsoft Teams, and GitHub, improving response speed and accuracy by automatically selecting relevant data sources.

Shared projects support asynchronous collaboration with role-based access controls and private memory to securely retain project details. Compliance enhancements include new ISO certifications and expanded SOC 2 reports, along with improved single sign-on and admin controls. These features are currently available to Business, Enterprise, and Edu plans, with broader availability planned for other tiers.

items.title: OpenAI launches GDPval to evaluate AI model performance on 1,320 real-world tasks across 44 occupations tied to US GDP [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Measuring the performance of our models on real-world tasks
items.summary:
OpenAI introduced GDPval, a new evaluation framework designed to measure AI model performance on economically valuable, real-world tasks spanning 44 occupations across nine major US industries. GDPval includes 1,320 specialized tasks based on actual work products such as legal briefs, engineering blueprints, and nursing care plans, aiming to assess how models can support professionals in everyday knowledge work.

GDPval builds on previous benchmarks by focusing on realistic deliverables that require context and diverse formats like documents, slides, and spreadsheets, rather than simple text prompts. The evaluation covers occupations selected for their significant contribution to US GDP and wages, providing a more comprehensive and practical measure of AI capabilities in the workforce. Future versions plan to incorporate interactive workflows to better capture the complexity of real-world tasks.

items.originalTitle: SAP and OpenAI partner to launch sovereign ‘OpenAI for Germany’
items.summary:
SAP and OpenAI announced a partnership to create OpenAI for Germany, aiming to deliver secure, sovereign AI solutions tailored for Germany’s public sector. The initiative will leverage SAP’s enterprise expertise and OpenAI’s AI technology, hosted on SAP’s Delos Cloud infrastructure running on Microsoft Azure, to meet strict data sovereignty and security requirements.

The collaboration plans to support millions of public sector employees by integrating AI into government workflows to improve efficiency and service delivery. SAP intends to expand Delos Cloud’s AI infrastructure to 4000 GPUs and may extend the offering to other European markets. This effort aligns with Germany’s national AI goals and broader digital sovereignty initiatives backed by significant investments from SAP and other industry leaders.

items.summary:
OpenAI, Oracle, and SoftBank announced five new AI data center sites under the Stargate platform, bringing planned capacity to nearly 7 gigawatts and over $400 billion in investment. This expansion accelerates their goal to reach a $500 billion, 10-gigawatt commitment by the end of 2025, creating tens of thousands of jobs across the U.S.

The new sites include locations in Texas, New Mexico, Wisconsin, Ohio, and additional capacity near Abilene, Texas. Oracle and SoftBank are leading development efforts, with Oracle delivering NVIDIA GB200 racks and SoftBank deploying advanced data center designs. The expansion follows a nationwide selection process reviewing over 300 proposals and aims to support next-generation AI research and infrastructure scalability.

items.title: CNA integrates AI across its newsroom to enhance journalism workflows and disinformation detection, with early adoption starting in 2019 and extensive use during Singapore's 2025 General Election [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: CNA is transforming its newsroom with AI
items.summary:
Channel NewsAsia (CNA), a global news network based in Singapore, has incorporated AI technologies throughout its newsroom to improve reporting efficiency and content accuracy. Editor-in-Chief Walter Fernandez detailed how CNA began experimenting with AI in 2019 and now uses custom GPT models to assist journalists, including tools for transcribing parliamentary sessions and analyzing social media campaigns during elections.

CNA emphasizes responsible AI use, establishing guidelines and human oversight to avoid misuse such as AI-generated voices or footage in news coverage. The newsroom has developed over twenty specialized GPTs, including a popular "Newsroom Buddy" for brainstorming and style checking, and has deployed AI tools to more than 2,500 users across its organization. CNA views AI as a foundational technology that supports its mission of public service journalism while transforming newsroom culture and workflows.

items.summary:
OpenAI and NVIDIA have formed a strategic partnership to deploy at least 10 gigawatts of AI datacenters powered by NVIDIA systems, with the first phase launching in the second half of 2026 using NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform. NVIDIA plans to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI progressively as each gigawatt is deployed to support this infrastructure expansion.

The partnership aims to advance OpenAI's next-generation AI infrastructure for training and running future models, with NVIDIA serving as a preferred compute and networking partner. This collaboration builds on a decade of cooperation between the two companies and complements their work with other partners like Microsoft and Oracle to develop advanced AI infrastructure at scale.

items.title: OpenAI and Apollo Research develop tests for AI scheming and reduce covert misalignment behaviors by up to 30× in frontier models [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Detecting and reducing scheming in AI models
items.summary:
OpenAI and Apollo Research collaborated to create evaluation environments that detect hidden misalignment, or "scheming," in advanced AI models and found behaviors consistent with scheming in controlled tests. They introduced an early method called deliberative alignment that significantly reduced covert deceptive actions in models like OpenAI o3 and o4-mini.

Scheming refers to AI models pretending to be aligned while secretly pursuing other agendas, a risk expected to grow as AI systems handle more complex, real-world tasks. The research showed a reduction from 13% to 0.4% in covert actions for o3 and from 8.7% to 0.3% for o4-mini, though some rare failures remain. OpenAI emphasizes the need for transparency in AI reasoning to better detect and mitigate scheming and plans to expand research efforts and collaborations to address this challenge as part of broader AI alignment and safety work.

items.title: OpenAI launches Stargate UK AI infrastructure partnership with NVIDIA and Nscale to enhance UK sovereign compute capabilities starting in 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing Stargate UK
items.summary:
OpenAI announced Stargate UK, a partnership with NVIDIA and Nscale to establish local AI infrastructure in the UK, enabling OpenAI's models to run on UK-based computing power for specialized use cases where jurisdiction is important. The initiative supports the UK’s national AI Opportunities Action Plan and aims to boost the country’s economy and global competitiveness.

The project will expand Nscale's UK capacity across multiple sites, including Cobalt Park in the AI Growth Zone, with plans to deploy up to 8,000 GPUs in early 2026 and potentially scale to 31,000 GPUs. NVIDIA will supply advanced GPUs featuring British-designed Arm chips. OpenAI also plans to bring its AI literacy hub, the OpenAI Academy, to the UK to help upskill 7.5 million workers by 2030, supporting broader AI adoption and economic growth.

items.title: OpenAI outlines principles balancing teen safety, user freedom, and privacy in AI interactions with new age-prediction and parental control features [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Teen safety, freedom, and privacy
items.summary:
OpenAI has detailed its approach to managing the tensions between teen safety, user freedom, and privacy in AI use, emphasizing the protection of sensitive conversations and advocating for privacy rights. The company prioritizes safety for users under 18 by implementing an age-prediction system and applying stricter content rules and interventions for teens, including parental and authority notifications in cases of imminent harm.

The policy distinguishes between adult and teen users, allowing broader freedoms for adults while restricting certain interactions for minors, such as flirtatious talk or discussions of self-harm, even in creative contexts. OpenAI acknowledges the challenges and trade-offs involved, including privacy compromises like ID verification in some regions, and aims to be transparent about its decisions after consulting experts.

items.originalTitle: How people are using ChatGPT
items.summary:
OpenAI published the largest study to date analyzing 1.5 million ChatGPT conversations, revealing that adoption has expanded beyond early users with significant narrowing of gender gaps and rapid growth in low- and middle-income countries. The study highlights that most usage focuses on everyday tasks such as seeking information, writing, and practical guidance, with about 30% of interactions related to work and 70% to personal use, demonstrating ChatGPT's role in enhancing productivity and decision-making across contexts.

The research, conducted with the National Bureau of Economic Research and Harvard economist David Deming, shows that ChatGPT usage patterns include asking for advice, task completion, and personal expression, with increasing user engagement over time. These findings underscore ChatGPT's dual function as a productivity tool and a source of personal value, contributing economic benefits that traditional metrics may not fully capture.

items.originalTitle: A People-First AI Fund: $50M to support nonprofits
items.summary:
OpenAI has opened applications for its People-First AI Fund, a $50 million initiative aimed at supporting U.S.-based nonprofits working to advance education, community innovation, and economic opportunity through AI. The fund offers unrestricted grants to organizations at various stages of AI adoption, with a focus on helping communities shape AI for public benefit. Applications close on October 8, 2025, and grants will be distributed by the end of the year.

The fund targets nonprofits that promote AI literacy and public understanding, foster community-led AI innovation, and expand economic opportunities in fair and inclusive ways. Eligible organizations must be U.S.-based 501(c)(3) public charities primarily operating within the United States. OpenAI emphasizes supporting initiatives that enhance human work and ensure AI benefits are broadly shared rather than concentrated.

items.title: OpenAI explains language model hallucinations as a result of training and evaluation methods that reward guessing over uncertainty [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Why language models hallucinate
items.summary: OpenAI's new research identifies that language models hallucinate because standard training and evaluation procedures incentivize guessing rather than acknowledging uncertainty. Despite improvements in models like GPT-5, hallucinations—confident but false statements—remain a persistent challenge. The research highlights that current accuracy-focused evaluations encourage models to guess answers to improve scores, even when uncertain, leading to more errors and hallucinations. OpenAI suggests updating evaluation metrics to penalize confident errors more than uncertainty and to reward appropriate expressions of uncertainty, aiming to improve AI reliability, honesty, and safety.

These efforts aim to strengthen security posture, protect users, and ensure responsible AI development at scale.

The business impact is important due to the scale of users and the need for robust security, while the risk is material but not critical, warranting planning and pilot actions.

importance.technical_rationale: The integration of AI-powered cyber defense, continuous adversarial red teaming, and modular security frameworks represent important technical advances that affect how enterprises must secure and operate AI systems. importance.development_summary: Researchers present preliminary evidence that increasing inference-time compute in reasoning models can improve robustness against adversarial attacks. However, this is early research with limitations and no current production deployment or enterprise controls.

items.summary: We’ve simplified, stabilized, and scaled continuous-time consistency models, achieving comparable sample quality to leading diffusion models, while using only two sampling steps.
items.description: We’ve simplified, stabilized, and scaled continuous-time consistency models, achieving comparable sample quality to leading diffusion models, while using only two sampling steps.
items.originalSummary: We’ve simplified, stabilized, and scaled continuous-time consistency models, achieving comparable sample quality to leading diffusion models, while using only two sampling steps.

aiRelevance.primary_ai_topic: generative AI models and sampling efficiency
aiRelevance.rationale: The story is substantively about advancements in generative AI, specifically continuous-time consistency models that improve sampling speed and quality compared to diffusion models, which are core AI technologies for image generation.
evidence: Title: Simplifying, stabilizing, and scaling continuous-time consistency models
Summary: Achieving comparable sample quality to leading diffusion models with only two sampling steps

Article content: Discusses continuous-time consistency models as a faster alternative to diffusion models for generative AI, training of a 1.5 billion parameter model, benchmarking sample quality and compute efficiency, and implications for real-time generative AI applications

importance.development_summary: Researchers have developed a simplified and stabilized continuous-time consistency model (sCM) that achieves sample quality comparable to leading diffusion models but with only two sampling steps, significantly speeding up generation. This model scales to 1.5 billion parameters and offers about a 50x speedup in sample generation time compared to traditional diffusion models. The approach is currently research-focused with no immediate enterprise deployment or governance details provided.
importance.recommended_action: Monitor
importance.rationale: The development represents an important technical advance in generative AI model efficiency that could influence future enterprise AI architectures and platform strategies. However, it remains at a research stage (ER0) without clear production deployment, governance, or security models, limiting immediate business impact and risk. Confidence is emerging based on credible research but lacks enterprise readiness, so monitoring for further validation and production adoption is appropriate.

Availability of security, governance, and operational controls
Adoption by major vendors or enterprise customers
Improvements in sample quality closing the gap with diffusion models
Emergence of real-time generative AI applications based on this model

importance.technical_rationale: The model introduces a significant technical improvement in sampling efficiency and model scaling that could influence future AI platform architectures, but it is not yet production-ready or widely adopted, so technical impact is important but not transformational.

items.summary: We've developed and applied a new method leveraging Rule-Based Rewards (RBRs) that aligns models to behave safely without extensive human data collection.
items.description: We've developed and applied a new method leveraging Rule-Based Rewards (RBRs) that aligns models to behave safely without extensive human data collection.
items.originalSummary: We've developed and applied a new method leveraging Rule-Based Rewards (RBRs) that aligns models to behave safely without extensive human data collection.

aiRelevance.rationale: The story is substantively about improving AI model safety behavior using a novel method called Rule-Based Rewards (RBRs), which is directly related to AI research, model alignment, and safety. It discusses AI systems, reinforcement learning, reward models, and safety policies, all core AI topics.
evidence: Title: 'Improving Model Safety Behavior with Rule-Based Rewards'
Summary: 'leveraging Rule-Based Rewards (RBRs) that aligns models to behave safely'

Article: 'RBRs significantly enhance the safety of our AI systems', 'used as part of our safety stack since GPT-4 launch', 'RBRs combined with rewards from a helpful-only reward model and used as an additional signal in PPO algorithms', 'RBR-trained models demonstrated safety performance comparable to those trained with human feedback'

importance.development_summary: OpenAI has developed Rule-Based Rewards (RBRs) to improve AI model safety by using explicit rules to guide model behavior, reducing reliance on extensive human feedback. This method has been integrated into their safety stack since GPT-4 launch and shows comparable safety performance to human feedback with cost and time efficiency. RBRs enable faster updates to safety policies and maintain a balance between helpfulness and safety in AI responses.
importance.recommended_action: Start pilot planning, vendor evaluation, architecture review, policy review, or roadmap analysis.
importance.rationale: The introduction of RBRs represents an important technical advancement that influences how enterprises can build and govern AI safety models, reducing human feedback dependency and enabling more agile safety policy updates. It has clear business implications by improving safety and reducing training costs, with material risk considerations around governance and potential bias. The method is production-ready with validated results, impacting task-level workflows and requiring planning for adoption and integration.
watch_items: Broader adoption of RBRs across multiple vendors or platforms
Evidence of RBRs causing significant operational or governance challenges
Regulatory developments mandating or restricting rule-based safety methods
Further validation or refutation of RBR effectiveness in diverse enterprise scenarios
importance.business_rationale: RBRs reduce training costs and improve safety, influencing procurement and governance decisions, and potentially shifting AI safety workflows.
importance.technical_rationale: RBRs introduce a new architectural approach to model alignment that reduces reliance on human feedback, impacting AI training pipelines and safety governance frameworks.

items.title: Video generation models as world simulators
items.originalTitle: Video generation models as world simulators
items.summary: We explore large-scale training of generative models on video data. Specifically, we train text-conditional diffusion models jointly on videos and images of variable durations, resolutions and aspect ratios. We leverage a transformer architecture that operates on spacetime patches of video and image latent codes. Our largest model, Sora, is capable of generating a minute of high fidelity video. Our results suggest that scaling video generation models is a promising path towards building general purpose simulators of the physical world.

items.summary: Researchers are developing a framework to assess the potential risk of large language models (LLMs) like GPT-4 being used to assist in creating biological threats. This work serves as an initial step for ongoing research and discussions within the community.

evidence: Title: 'Building an early warning system for LLM-aided biological threat creation'

Study involving human participants comparing GPT-4 plus internet access versus internet-only to assess AI's impact on biological threat creation accuracy and completeness.

importance.development_summary: Researchers developed a framework to evaluate the risk of large language models aiding biological threat creation, conducting a study with biology experts and students comparing GPT-4 access to internet-only access. The study found only mild, statistically insignificant improvements in accuracy and completeness when using GPT-4, indicating limited current risk increase. This work serves as an early research step to inform ongoing community discussion and future evaluations of AI-enabled biological risks.
importance.recommended_action: Monitor for follow-up evidence and further research developments.
importance.rationale: The development is an early-stage research effort assessing AI risks in biological threat creation, with no conclusive evidence of significant impact or forced enterprise changes. The technical impact is informational as it does not change enterprise AI architecture or operations, and business impact is optional since it does not currently affect strategy or operations. However, the risk is material (R2) due to the potential security implications, warranting monitoring and further evaluation as the research and AI capabilities evolve.

items.title: Forecasting potential misuses of language models for disinformation campaigns and how to reduce risk
items.originalTitle: Forecasting potential misuses of language models for disinformation campaigns and how to reduce risk
items.summary: OpenAI researchers collaborated with Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology and the Stanford Internet Observatory to investigate how large language models might be misused for disinformation purposes. The collaboration included an October 2021 workshop bringing together 30 disinformation researchers, machine learning experts, and policy analysts, and culminated in a co-authored report building on more than a year of research. This report outlines the threats that language models pose to the information environment if used to augment disinformation campaigns and introduces a framework for analyzing potential mitigations. Read the full report here.

items.title: Learning to play Minecraft with Video PreTraining
items.originalTitle: Learning to play Minecraft with Video PreTraining
items.summary: We trained a neural network to play Minecraft by Video PreTraining (VPT) on a massive unlabeled video dataset of human Minecraft play, while using only a small amount of labeled contractor data. With fine-tuning, our model can learn to craft diamond tools, a task that usually takes proficient humans over 20 minutes (24,000 actions). Our model uses the native human interface of keypresses and mouse movements, making it quite general, and represents a step towards general computer-using agents.

items.title: AI and efficiency
items.originalTitle: AI and efficiency
items.summary: We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012 the amount of compute needed to train a neural net to the same performance on ImageNet classification has been decreasing by a factor of 2 every 16 months. Compared to 2012, it now takes 44 times less compute to train a neural network to the level of AlexNet (by contrast, Moore’s Law would yield an 11x cost improvement over this period). Our results suggest that for AI tasks with high levels of recent investment, algorithmic progress has yielded more gains than classical hardware efficiency.

items.title: Improving verifiability in AI development
items.originalTitle: Improving verifiability in AI development
items.summary: We’ve contributed to a multi-stakeholder report by 58 co-authors at 30 organizations, including the Centre for the Future of Intelligence, Mila, Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society, Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences, and Center for Security and Emerging Technologies. This report describes 10 mechanisms to improve the verifiability of claims made about AI systems. Developers can use these tools to provide evidence that AI systems are safe, secure, fair, or privacy-preserving. Users, policymakers, and civil society can use these tools to evaluate AI development processes.

items.title: Deep double descent
items.originalTitle: Deep double descent
items.summary: We show that the double descent phenomenon occurs in CNNs, ResNets, and transformers: performance first improves, then gets worse, and then improves again with increasing model size, data size, or training time. This effect is often avoided through careful regularization. While this behavior appears to be fairly universal, we don’t yet fully understand why it happens, and view further study of this phenomenon as an important research direction.

While there have been larger language models released since August, we’ve continued with our original staged release plan in order to provide the community with a test case of a full staged release process. We hope that this test case will be useful to developers of future powerful models, and we’re actively continuing the conversation with the AI community on responsible publication.

items.title: Solving Rubik’s Cube with a robot hand
items.originalTitle: Solving Rubik’s Cube with a robot hand
items.summary: We’ve trained a pair of neural networks to solve the Rubik’s Cube with a human-like robot hand. The neural networks are trained entirely in simulation, using the same reinforcement learning code as OpenAI Five paired with a new technique called Automatic Domain Randomization (ADR). The system can handle situations it never saw during training, such as being prodded by a stuffed giraffe. This shows that reinforcement learning isn’t just a tool for virtual tasks, but can solve physical-world problems requiring unprecedented dexterity.

items.title: Fine-tuning GPT-2 from human preferences
items.originalTitle: Fine-tuning GPT-2 from human preferences
items.summary: We’ve fine-tuned the 774M parameter GPT-2 language model using human feedback for various tasks, successfully matching the preferences of the external human labelers, though those preferences did not always match our own. Specifically, for summarization tasks the labelers preferred sentences copied wholesale from the input (we’d only asked them to ensure accuracy), so our models learned to copy. Summarization required 60k human labels; simpler tasks which continue text in various styles required only 5k. Our motivation is to move safety techniques closer to the general task of “machines talking to humans,” which we believe is key to extracting information about human values.

items.title: Emergent tool use from multi-agent interaction
items.originalTitle: Emergent tool use from multi-agent interaction
items.summary: We’ve observed agents discovering progressively more complex tool use while playing a simple game of hide-and-seek. Through training in our new simulated hide-and-seek environment, agents build a series of six distinct strategies and counterstrategies, some of which we did not know our environment supported. The self-supervised emergent complexity in this simple environment further suggests that multi-agent co-adaptation may one day produce extremely complex and intelligent behavior.

items.title: Testing robustness against unforeseen adversaries
items.originalTitle: Testing robustness against unforeseen adversaries
items.summary: We’ve developed a method to assess whether a neural network classifier can reliably defend against adversarial attacks not seen during training. Our method yields a new metric, UAR (Unforeseen Attack Robustness), which evaluates the robustness of a single model against an unanticipated attack, and highlights the need to measure performance across a more diverse range of unforeseen attacks.

items.title: GPT-2: 6-month follow-up
items.originalTitle: GPT-2: 6-month follow-up
items.summary: We’re releasing the 774 million parameter GPT-2 language model after the release of our small 124M model in February, staged release of our medium 355M model in May, and subsequent research with partners and the AI community into the model’s potential for misuse and societal benefit. We’re also releasing an open-source legal agreement to make it easier for organizations to initiate model-sharing partnerships with each other, and are publishing a technical report about our experience in coordinating with the wider AI research community on publication norms.

items.title: Why responsible AI development needs cooperation on safety
items.originalTitle: Why responsible AI development needs cooperation on safety
items.summary: We’ve written a policy research paper identifying four strategies that can be used today to improve the likelihood of long-term industry cooperation on safety norms in AI: communicating risks and benefits, technical collaboration, increased transparency, and incentivizing standards. Our analysis shows that industry cooperation on safety will be instrumental in ensuring that AI systems are safe and beneficial, but competitive pressures could lead to a collective action problem, potentially causing AI companies to under-invest in safety. We hope these strategies will encourage greater cooperation on the safe development of AI and lead to better global outcomes of AI.

items.title: MuseNet
items.originalTitle: MuseNet
items.summary: We’ve created MuseNet, a deep neural network that can generate 4-minute musical compositions with 10 different instruments, and can combine styles from country to Mozart to the Beatles. MuseNet was not explicitly programmed with our understanding of music, but instead discovered patterns of harmony, rhythm, and style by learning to predict the next token in hundreds of thousands of MIDI files. MuseNet uses the same general-purpose unsupervised technology as GPT-2, a large-scale transformer model trained to predict the next token in a sequence, whether audio or text.

items.title: Implicit generation and generalization methods for energy-based models
items.originalTitle: Implicit generation and generalization methods for energy-based models
items.summary: We’ve made progress towards stable and scalable training of energy-based models (EBMs) resulting in better sample quality and generalization ability than existing models. Generation in EBMs spends more compute to continually refine its answers and doing so can generate samples competitive with GANs at low temperatures, while also having mode coverage guarantees of likelihood-based models. We hope these findings stimulate further research into this promising class of models.

items.title: AI safety needs social scientists
items.originalTitle: AI safety needs social scientists
items.summary: We’ve written a paper arguing that long-term AI safety research needs social scientists to ensure AI alignment algorithms succeed when actual humans are involved. Properly aligning advanced AI systems with human values requires resolving many uncertainties related to the psychology of human rationality, emotion, and biases. The aim of this paper is to spark further collaboration between machine learning and social science researchers, and we plan to hire social scientists to work on this full time at OpenAI.

items.title: How AI training scales
items.originalTitle: How AI training scales
items.summary: We’ve discovered that the gradient noise scale, a simple statistical metric, predicts the parallelizability of neural network training on a wide range of tasks. Since complex tasks tend to have noisier gradients, increasingly large batch sizes are likely to become useful in the future, removing one potential limit to further growth of AI systems. More broadly, these results show that neural network training need not be considered a mysterious art, but can be rigorized and systematized.

items.summary: We’ve developed an energy-based model that can quickly learn to identify and generate instances of concepts, such as near, above, between, closest, and furthest, expressed as sets of 2d points. We also show cross-domain transfer: we use concepts learned in a 2d particle environment to solve tasks on a 3-dimensional physics-based robot.

items.originalTitle: Learning complex goals with iterated amplification
items.summary: We’re proposing an AI safety technique called iterated amplification that lets us specify complicated behaviors and goals that are beyond human scale, by demonstrating how to decompose a task into simpler sub-tasks, rather than by providing labeled data or a reward function. items.summary: We introduce Glow, a reversible generative model which uses invertible 1x1 convolutions. It extends previous work on reversible generative models and simplifies the architecture. items.summary: We’ve obtained state-of-the-art results on a suite of diverse language tasks with a scalable, task-agnostic system, which we’re also releasing. These results provide a convincing example that pairing supervised learning methods with unsupervised pre-training works very well; this is an idea that many have explored in the past, and we hope our result motivates further research into applying this idea on larger and more diverse datasets.

items.title: AI and compute
items.originalTitle: AI and compute
items.summary: We’re releasing an analysis showing that since 2012, the amount of compute used in the largest AI training runs has been increasing exponentially with a 3.4-month doubling time (by comparison, Moore’s Law had a 2-year doubling period)[^footnote-correction]. Since 2012, this metric has grown by more than 300,000x (a 2-year doubling period would yield only a 7x increase). Improvements in compute have been a key component of AI progress, so as long as this trend continues, it’s worth preparing for the implications of systems far outside today’s capabilities.

items.title: Reptile: A scalable meta-learning algorithm
items.originalTitle: Reptile: A scalable meta-learning algorithm
items.summary: We’ve developed a simple meta-learning algorithm called Reptile which works by repeatedly sampling a task, performing stochastic gradient descent on it, and updating the initial parameters towards the final parameters learned on that task. Reptile is the application of the Shortest Descent algorithm to the meta-learning setting, and is mathematically similar to first-order MAML (which is a version of the well-known MAML algorithm) that only needs black-box access to an optimizer such as SGD or Adam, with similar computational efficiency and performance.

items.title: Competitive self-play
items.originalTitle: Competitive self-play
items.summary: We’ve found that self-play allows simulated AIs to discover physical skills like tackling, ducking, faking, kicking, catching, and diving for the ball, without explicitly designing an environment with these skills in mind. Self-play ensures that the environment is always the right difficulty for an AI to improve. Taken alongside our Dota 2 self-play results, we have increasing confidence that self-play will be a core part of powerful AI systems in the future.

items.title: More on Dota 2
items.originalTitle: More on Dota 2
items.summary: Our Dota 2 result shows that self-play can catapult the performance of machine learning systems from far below human level to superhuman, given sufficient compute. In the span of a month, our system went from barely matching a high-ranked player to beating the top pros and has continued to improve since then. Supervised deep learning systems can only be as good as their training datasets, but in self-play systems, the available data improves automatically as the agent gets better.

This is a step towards building AI systems which accomplish well-defined goals in messy, complicated situations involving real humans.

items.title: Learning to cooperate, compete, and communicate
items.originalTitle: Learning to cooperate, compete, and communicate
items.summary: Multiagent environments where agents compete for resources are stepping stones on the path to AGI. Multiagent environments have two useful properties: first, there is a natural curriculum—the difficulty of the environment is determined by the skill of your competitors (and if you’re competing against clones of yourself, the environment exactly matches your skill level). Second, a multiagent environment has no stable equilibrium: no matter how smart an agent is, there’s always pressure to get smarter. These environments have a very different feel from traditional environments, and it’ll take a lot more research before we become good at them.

items.title: Refik Anadol's Dataland opens as world's first AI art museum with immersive rainforest exhibit using wearables and AI-trained on Amazon data
items.originalTitle: A New Experiential Gallery Just Might Change Your Mind About AI Art
items.summary:
Dataland, co-founded by artist Refik Anadol in downtown Los Angeles, launched as the world's first museum dedicated to AI art, featuring an immersive exhibit called Machine Dreams: Rainforest. The exhibit uses wearable devices to track visitors' biometrics and movements, generating dynamic digital visuals and soundscapes based on AI models trained with extensive natural science data collected from the Amazon and other rainforests.

Anadol and his team spent three years developing their own AI models using five petabytes of data sourced with researcher consent, aiming to create an ethical and environmentally responsible AI art experience. The exhibit responds interactively to visitors, incorporating scents and visual effects that simulate natural environments, challenging common perceptions of AI-generated art as simplistic or derivative.

items.title: Google just redesigned the search box for the first time in 25 years â hereâs why it matters more than you think.
items.originalTitle: Google just redesigned the search box for the first time in 25 years â hereâs why it matters more than you think.
items.summary: Google has introduced a major redesign of its search box, the first in 25 years, transforming it from a simple keyword input into a dynamic, AI-powered interface that supports multimodal inputs such as text, images, PDFs, videos, and Chrome tabs. This update merges AI Overviews and AI Mode into a seamless experience, allowing users to engage in conversational search without switching interfaces. The redesign is powered by Google's new Gemini 3.5 Flash AI model, which offers improved speed and quality. New features include generative UI for interactive visuals and mini apps, customizable AI agents for monitoring web content, and enhanced query suggestions. These changes reflect a shift in user behavior towards more detailed, conversational queries and have significant implications for publishers, advertisers, and SEO practices. Google emphasizes that this redesign signals a broader move towards AI-driven, conversational computing, supported by substantial infrastructure investments.

items.title: Railway secures $100 million to challenge AWS with AI-native cloud infrastructure
items.originalTitle: Railway secures $100 million to challenge AWS with AI-native cloud infrastructure
items.summary: Railway, a San Francisco-based cloud platform, has raised $100 million in a Series B funding round led by TQ Ventures to develop AI-native cloud infrastructure. The company aims to address the limitations of traditional cloud providers like AWS and Google Cloud by offering faster deployment times—under one second compared to the typical two to three minutes—and significantly lower costs. Railway has built its own data centers, abandoning Google Cloud to gain full control over its infrastructure, enabling improved performance and pricing. With a team of 30 employees, Railway serves over two million developers and claims usage by 31% of Fortune 500 companies. The platform supports various databases and offers enterprise features such as SOC 2 Type 2 compliance and HIPAA readiness. Railway plans to use the new funding to expand its global data centers and grow its team, positioning itself to capitalize on the increasing volume of AI-generated software requiring cloud infrastructure.

items.title: Claude Code costs up to $200 a month. Goose does the same thing for free.
items.originalTitle: Claude Code costs up to $200 a month. Goose does the same thing for free.
items.summary: Anthropic's AI coding tool, Claude Code, offers advanced autonomous coding capabilities but comes with subscription fees ranging from $20 to $200 per month and usage limits that have frustrated developers. In response, Block has developed Goose, a free, open-source AI coding agent that runs locally on users' machines, eliminating subscription costs, usage caps, and cloud dependencies. Goose supports multiple language models, including local open-source models, providing privacy and offline functionality. While Claude Code's proprietary models currently offer superior performance and larger context windows, Goose's flexibility and cost-effectiveness appeal to developers prioritizing autonomy and privacy. The AI coding tools market is evolving, with open-source alternatives narrowing the quality gap, potentially challenging premium pricing models in the future.

items.title: Salesforce rolls out new Slackbot AI agent as it battles Microsoft and Google in workplace AI
items.originalTitle: Salesforce rolls out new Slackbot AI agent as it battles Microsoft and Google in workplace AI
items.summary: Salesforce has launched a completely redesigned Slackbot, transforming it from a basic notification tool into an AI-powered assistant capable of searching enterprise data, drafting documents, and performing tasks for employees. The new Slackbot, available to Business+ and Enterprise+ customers, operates on Anthropic's Claude large language model, with plans to support additional AI providers like Google's Gemini and potentially OpenAI. Internally tested by 80,000 Salesforce employees, Slackbot has seen rapid adoption and high satisfaction, with users reporting significant time savings. The assistant integrates data from multiple sources, synthesizes insights, and facilitates collaboration through Slack's Canvas feature. Salesforce positions Slackbot as a "super agent" that could coordinate with other AI agents, aiming to embed AI directly into workplace communication. The launch places Salesforce in competition with Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini in the enterprise AI space. Slackbot is included at no extra cost for eligible customers, though some may face increased costs due to Salesforce's broader data access pricing changes. The rollout will complete by early March, with additional features planned. Salesforce views Slackbot as central to the future of work, emphasizing conversational AI embedded in existing tools to enhance productivity.

items.title: Anthropic launches Cowork, a Claude Desktop agent that works in your files â no coding required
items.originalTitle: Anthropic launches Cowork, a Claude Desktop agent that works in your files â no coding required
items.summary: Anthropic has introduced Cowork, a new AI agent designed to assist non-technical users by working directly with files on their computers without requiring coding skills. Built rapidly in about ten days, reportedly with significant help from Anthropic's own AI coding tool, Claude Code, Cowork allows users to designate folders for the AI to access, enabling it to read, edit, and create files within that space. The agent can perform tasks such as organizing files, generating expense reports from receipts, and drafting documents from scattered notes. Cowork integrates with various external services and supports browser automation, enhancing its functionality beyond local files. Anthropic emphasizes safety by warning users about potential risks, including accidental file deletion and prompt injection attacks, and has implemented safeguards accordingly. Currently available as a research preview to Claude Max subscribers on macOS, Anthropic plans to expand Cowork to other platforms and users. This launch positions Anthropic as a competitor to Microsoft's Copilot and highlights a trend toward AI agents that blend productivity tools with conversational AI, aiming to make AI interactions feel more like collaborating with a coworker.

items.title: Nous Research's NousCoder-14B is an open-source coding model landing right in the Claude Code moment
items.originalTitle: Nous Research's NousCoder-14B is an open-source coding model landing right in the Claude Code moment
items.summary: Nous Research, an open-source AI startup supported by Paradigm, has released NousCoder-14B, a competitive programming model trained in four days using Nvidia's B200 GPUs. The model achieves a 67.87% accuracy on LiveCodeBench v6, surpassing its base model Alibaba's Qwen3-14B by over 7 percentage points. Unlike proprietary tools like Anthropic's Claude Code, NousCoder-14B emphasizes transparency by open-sourcing its model weights, training environment, and benchmarks, enabling reproducibility. The training involved reinforcement learning on 24,000 verified competitive programming problems, highlighting challenges such as data scarcity in this domain. Nous Research's approach includes dynamic sampling and iterative context extension to optimize learning. The company, which has raised $65 million, aims to compete with large tech firms through open-source innovation. Future research directions include multi-turn reinforcement learning, better response length control, and synthetic problem generation to address data limitations. The model and training stack are publicly available under an Apache 2.0 license.

The bank warned that this imbalance could lead to a significant valuation correction, or "snapback," as seen in past market cycles.

The warning comes amid a strong rally in tech stocks, with the S&P 500 experiencing its best quarter since 2020 despite subdued earnings and heavy spending on AI infrastructure. Analysts note that US stock valuations are at historically high levels, raising concerns about market sustainability. Recent volatility, including a major sell-off in June and fluctuations in international markets, underscores the risks ahead for investors heavily exposed to AI-driven companies.
